gems.line: The verse states His power, then closes in His mercy - the Forgiving, the Merciful holds both.

lines.text: My servant keeps drawing near to Me with voluntary acts until I love him...
Pharaoh did not run out of mercy; he ran out of moments when a yes could mean anything.
Only one city ever turned in time; this surah carries its prophet's name as the proof.

10:107.morning: Whatever touches you today is already sorted by the verse: harm only He removes, good none can block.
10:107.night: Whatever hurt today has only one remover - and He ends the verse as the Forgiving, the Merciful.

11:6.arabic: ۞ وَمَا مِن دَآبَّةٍۢ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ رِزْقُهَا وَيَعْلَمُ مُسْتَقَرَّهَا وَمُسْتَوْدَعَهَا ۚ كُلٌّۭ فِى كِتَٰبٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
11:6.translation: There is no animal on the earth, but that its sustenance lies with Allah, and He knows its [enduring] abode and its temporary place of lodging. Everything is in a manifest Book.

gems.title: Divine Sustenance
gems.insight: Every creature on earth has its provision guaranteed by Allah - no living being is forgotten or left without sustenance.
gems.line: No living thing is left off His provision - you were never in danger of being the exception.

gems.title: Clear Record
gems.insight: Allah knows each creature's 'dwelling place and storage place' - where it lives and where it will be buried, all recorded in a clear register.
gems.line: Where each creature dwells and where it comes to rest - all recorded in a clear register.

gems.title: Nothing Excluded
gems.insight: The phrase 'no creature on earth' (ma min dabbah) means Allah's care extends to all living things - from humans to the smallest insects.
gems.line: From the smallest insect upward, His care excludes nothing that moves upon the earth.

lines.text: Hud and its sisters have grayed me.
The same surah that grayed the Prophet was built, story by story, to steady his heart.
Fear needs a second power. Hud counted the powers in the world and came to one.

11:6.morning: Provision for every creature on earth is upon Allah - today's sustenance is already His to carry.
11:6.night: Every creature fed today was fed from Him - and tomorrow's provision sits in the same clear register.

11:123.arabic: وَلِلَّهِ غَيْبُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُ ٱلْأَمْرُ كُلُّهُۥ فَٱعْبُدْهُ وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَيْهِ ۚ وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
11:123.translation: To Allah belongs the Unseen of the heavens and the earth, and to Him all matters are returned. So worship Him and trust in Him. Your Lord is not oblivious of what you do.

gems.title: Allah's Domain
gems.insight: 'To Allah belong the unseen aspects of the heavens and the earth' establishes that all hidden knowledge - past, present, future - belongs exclusively to Allah.
gems.line: All that is hidden - in the heavens, the earth, and this day - is His domain, completely known.

gems.title: Return to Him
gems.insight: 'To Him will be returned the matter, all of it' means every affair, dispute, and question ultimately returns to Allah for final judgment and resolution.
gems.line: Every matter, all of it, returns to Him - no loose end of your life resolves anywhere else.

gems.title: Pure Worship
gems.insight: 'So worship Him' (fa'budhu) is the logical conclusion - since Allah owns all knowledge and all returns to Him, He alone deserves worship.
gems.line: Worship follows logically - the One who holds all knowledge and every outcome deserves it alone.

gems.title: Trust Him
gems.insight: 'Rely upon Him' (tawakkal 'alayhi) means complete trust - after understanding Allah's sovereignty and knowledge, we can confidently depend on Him for all affairs.
gems.line: Tawakkul is trust with reasons - knowing Who holds every affair makes reliance the sound response.

gems.title: Allah Sees All
gems.insight: 'Your Lord is not unaware of that which you do' (ma rabbuka bi-ghafilin) assures us that Allah observes every action - nothing escapes His attention or judgment.
gems.line: Your Lord is not unaware of what you do - effort nobody saw today was never actually unseen.

lines.text: Hud and its sisters have grayed me.
The same surah that grayed the Prophet was built, story by story, to steady his heart.
Fear needs a second power. Hud counted the powers in the world and came to one.

11:123.morning: Today's unseen belongs to Him and every matter returns to Him - so the verse says: worship, and rely.
11:123.night: Tomorrow's unseen is already His - and the One you leaned on today is not unaware of any of it.

14:12.arabic: وَمَا لَنَآ أَلَّا نَتَوَكَّلَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ وَقَدْ هَدَىٰنَا سُبُلَنَا ۚ وَلَنَصْبِرَنَّ عَلَىٰ مَآ ءَاذَيْتُمُونَا ۚ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ
14:12.translation: And why should we not put our trust in Allah, seeing that He has guided us in our ways? Surely, we will put up patiently with whatever torment you may inflict upon us, and in Allah let all the trusting put their trust.’

gems.title: Why Not Rely?
gems.insight: The messengers ask 'Why should we not rely on Allah?' - a rhetorical question emphasizing that reliance on the One who guided you is the only logical response.
gems.line: For the messengers, reliance on the One who guided them was simply the logical response.

gems.title: Guided to Good Ways
gems.insight: The messengers cite 'while He has guided us to our good ways' as proof that Allah deserves complete trust - past guidance guarantees future support.
gems.line: Past guidance is the messengers' proof for present trust - He who led you this far can be leaned on.

gems.title: Patience Against Harm
gems.insight: The messengers vow 'we will surely be patient against whatever harm you cause us,' showing that reliance includes perseverance through opposition.
gems.line: Their reliance included a vow of patience under harm - tawakkul stands firm through opposition.

gems.title: Emphatic Repetition
gems.insight: The verse repeats 'upon Allah let those who would rely indeed rely' for emphasis - tawakkul deserves constant reinforcement and practice.
gems.line: 'Upon Allah let the reliant rely' - repeated for emphasis, because trust needs constant renewing.

lines.text: A good word is like a good tree: its root is firm, and its branch reaches into the sky.
I am the prayer of my father Ibrahim.
What is planted with God in dead ground is never wasted; it grows while you are gone.

14:12.morning: The messengers saw no reason not to rely on Allah - He had guided them, and that was proof enough for trust.
14:12.night: The messengers' reasoning holds tonight: the One who guided you today can be trusted with tomorrow.

20:46.arabic: قَالَ لَا تَخَافَآ ۖ إِنَّنِى مَعَكُمَآ أَسْمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ
20:46.translation: He said, ‘Do not be afraid, for I will be with the two of you, hearing and seeing [whatever happens].

gems.title: Divine Presence
gems.insight: Allah assures Moses and Aaron with 'I am with you both; I hear and I see' - a promise of divine presence that transcends physical proximity. This companionship means Allah's awareness, protection, and support in the most daunting mission.
gems.line: 'I am with you' meant awareness, protection, and support - a presence no distance interrupts.

gems.title: Fear Not
gems.insight: The command 'Fear not' (لَا تَخَافَآ) precedes the mission to confront Pharaoh. Faith-based courage isn't the absence of fear but acting despite it, anchored in trust in Allah's promise.
gems.line: 'Fear not' came before the hardest mission - courage in faith is acting while fear is still real.

gems.title: All-Hearing, All-Seeing
gems.insight: Allah's attributes of hearing (أَسْمَعُ) and seeing (أَرَىٰ) aren't passive observation but active engagement. He hears every word of the oppressor and sees every act of the oppressed.
gems.line: His hearing and seeing are active - every word of the oppressor, every act against the oppressed.

lines.text: O God, You are my trust in every distress, and my hope in every hardship.
And when you have resolved, rely upon God. Indeed God loves those who rely.
Trust placed in Him, not in the outcome, cannot be broken by the outcome.

20:46.morning: Musa and Harun walked toward Pharaoh on one assurance: 'I am with you both; I hear and I see.'
20:46.night: The One who told Musa 'I hear and I see' missed nothing of today - not a word, not an act.

25:58.arabic: وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱلْحَىِّ ٱلَّذِى لَا يَمُوتُ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِهِۦ ۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِهِۦ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِۦ خَبِيرًا
25:58.translation: Put your trust in the Living One who does not die, and celebrate His praise. He suffices as one all-aware of the sins of His servants.

gems.title: Ever-Living
gems.insight: Command to rely on al-hayy alladhi la yamut (the Ever-Living who does not die) - unique attribute distinguishing Allah from all creation.
gems.line: Al-Hayy alladhi la yamut - the one refuge that cannot be outlived stands apart from all creation.

gems.title: Constant Glorification
gems.insight: Command to 'sabbih bi-hamdihi' (exalt with His praise) - glorification coupled with gratitude, combining transcendence acknowledgment with blessing recognition.
gems.line: Glorifying joined with praise - awe at what He is, thanks for what He gives, in a single breath.

gems.title: All-Aware Judge
gems.insight: Verse ends with 'kafa bihi bi-dhunubi 'ibadihi khabiran' (sufficient is He, Acquainted with the sins of His servants) - total divine awareness of human failures.
gems.line: He is fully Acquainted with His servants' sins - nothing needs reporting, and nothing is missed.

lines.text: O God, You are my trust in every distress, and my hope in every hardship.
And when you have resolved, rely upon God. Indeed God loves those who rely.
Trust placed in Him, not in the outcome, cannot be broken by the outcome.

25:58.morning: Everything you might lean on today can fail except One - the Ever-Living who does not die.
25:58.night: You can release the day into hands that never weaken - the Ever-Living who does not die keeps the night.

26:62.arabic: قَالَ كَلَّآ ۖ إِنَّ مَعِىَ رَبِّى سَيَهْدِينِ
26:62.translation: He said, ‘Certainly not! Indeed my Lord is with me. He will guide me.’

gems.title: Prophetic Certainty
gems.insight: Moses responds with absolute certainty: 'No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.' This contrasts sharply with the people's fear, showing the prophet's unwavering trust.
gems.line: The people saw capture; Musa saw his Lord - certainty can stand beside panic and hold.

gems.title: My Lord is With Me
gems.insight: 'Ma'iya Rabbi' (my Lord is with me) expresses the intimate divine presence. Moses doesn't say 'Allah will save us' but emphasizes personal, immediate divine companionship.
gems.line: 'With me is my Lord' - not distant rescue but companionship, personal and present inside the crisis.

gems.title: Divine Guidance
gems.insight: 'Sayahdin' (He will guide me) shows Moses didn't have the plan yet - but he had absolute trust that guidance would come at the right moment.
gems.line: Musa had no plan yet, only trust - guidance arrives at the moment it is needed, not before.

gems.title: Kalla - No!
gems.insight: Moses begins with 'Kalla' (No!) - a firm rejection of despair. Before offering reassurance, he firmly refuses to accept the premise of defeat.
gems.line: His first word was No - the premise of despair can be refused before any answer exists.

lines.text: O God, You are my trust in every distress, and my hope in every hardship.
And when you have resolved, rely upon God. Indeed God loves those who rely.
Trust placed in Him, not in the outcome, cannot be broken by the outcome.

26:62.morning: Whatever backs you into a corner today, Musa's answer stands ready: my Lord is with me; He will guide me.
26:62.night: Nothing had parted yet when Musa spoke his trust - the words still hold tonight: He will guide me.

27:79.arabic: فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَى ٱلْحَقِّ ٱلْمُبِينِ
27:79.translation: So put your trust in Allah, for you indeed stand on the manifest truth.

gems.title: Rely on Allah
gems.insight: The command to 'rely upon Allah' (tawakkul) is directly connected to standing on clear truth - confidence in Allah enables courage in proclaiming truth.
gems.line: Reliance on Allah is what makes truth speakable - confidence in Him comes first, courage follows.

gems.title: Manifest Truth
gems.insight: The phrase 'clear truth' (al-haqq al-mubin) emphasizes that the Prophet's message is self-evident and undeniable to those who examine it honestly.
gems.line: The message he carried is called clear truth - examined honestly, it shows itself.

gems.title: Prophet's Assurance
gems.insight: This verse directly addresses and reassures the Prophet Muhammad during opposition, affirming that he stands on unshakeable truth regardless of others' rejection.
gems.line: This was said to steady the Prophet under rejection - truth does not shake when people turn away.

lines.text: O God, You are my trust in every distress, and my hope in every hardship.
And when you have resolved, rely upon God. Indeed God loves those who rely.
Trust placed in Him, not in the outcome, cannot be broken by the outcome.

27:79.morning: The Prophet was told to rely on Allah because he stood on clear truth - trust and truth travel together.
27:79.night: Rejection never moved the Prophet from clear truth - what you stood on honestly today still stands tonight.

29:60.arabic: وَكَأَيِّن مِّن دَآبَّةٍۢ لَّا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا ٱللَّهُ يَرْزُقُهَا وَإِيَّاكُمْ ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
29:60.translation: How many an animal there is that does not carry its own provision. Allah provides them and you, and He is the All-hearing, the All-knowing.

gems.title: Divine Provision
gems.insight: Many creatures do not carry their own provision - yet Allah sustains them, proving that sustenance comes from divine will, not personal effort alone.
gems.line: Creatures that store nothing still eat - provision is His doing before it is yours.

gems.title: Natural Lessons
gems.insight: Animals and creatures serve as living examples (dabbah) of complete trust in Allah's provision, living without anxiety about tomorrow.
gems.line: Every unworried bird is a lesson in trust - living today without carrying tomorrow.

gems.title: All-Hearing, All-Knowing
gems.insight: Allah is As-Sami' (The Hearing) and Al-'Alim (The Knowing) - He hears our needs and knows our circumstances before we even express them.
gems.line: He is the Hearing, the Knowing - your need reached Him before you found words for it.

lines.text: O God, You are my trust in every distress, and my hope in every hardship.
And when you have resolved, rely upon God. Indeed God loves those who rely.
Trust placed in Him, not in the outcome, cannot be broken by the outcome.

29:60.morning: Countless creatures woke today carrying no provision - He will feed them, and you.
29:60.night: Everything that ate today was fed by Him - your tomorrow rests with the same Provider.

31:22.arabic: ۞ وَمَن يُسْلِمْ وَجْهَهُۥٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌۭ فَقَدِ ٱسْتَمْسَكَ بِٱلْعُرْوَةِ ٱلْوُثْقَىٰ ۗ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْأُمُورِ
31:22.translation: Whoever surrenders his heart to Allah and is virtuous, has certainly held fast to the firmest handle, and with Allah lies the outcome of all matters.

gems.title: Total Submission
gems.insight: Submitting one's 'face' (wajh) to Allah means complete surrender - the face represents identity and direction in life.
gems.line: Submitting the face means the whole of you - identity and direction turned toward Allah.

gems.title: Ihsan Required
gems.insight: Submission must be paired with ihsan (excellence in good deeds). Faith without righteous action is incomplete.
gems.line: Surrender travels with excellence - submission 'while a doer of good' is the verse's full picture.

gems.title: Al-Urwah Al-Wuthqa
gems.insight: The 'most trustworthy handhold' is an unbreakable connection to Allah through submission and good deeds - it never fails.
gems.line: Al-urwah al-wuthqa does not snap - the handhold of submission and good deeds never fails its holder.

gems.title: Final Return
gems.insight: All matters ultimately return (aqibah) to Allah. He is the final destination and judge of all affairs.
gems.line: Every unsettled matter is already addressed - to Allah is the outcome of all affairs.

lines.text: O God, You are my trust in every distress, and my hope in every hardship.
And when you have resolved, rely upon God. Indeed God loves those who rely.
Trust placed in Him, not in the outcome, cannot be broken by the outcome.

31:22.morning: Whoever submits his face to Allah while doing good has grasped the surest handhold - open again today.
31:22.night: Whatever stayed unresolved tonight is still traveling - to Allah is the outcome of all matters.

33:3.arabic: وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ وَكِيلًۭا
33:3.translation: And put your trust in Allah; Allah suffices as trustee.

gems.title: Complete Trust
gems.insight: Tawakkul (reliance upon Allah) is commanded as the foundational attitude for facing challenges. It means taking action while entrusting outcomes entirely to Allah.
gems.line: Tawakkul is acting while entrusting outcomes to Him - effort and reliance in one motion.

gems.title: Divine Sufficiency
gems.insight: Allah declares Himself sufficient as a Wakil (Disposer of affairs), meaning He alone is enough to manage all matters for those who trust in Him.
gems.line: Wakil is His self-declared role - He alone is enough to manage what is beyond you.

gems.title: Powerful Brevity
gems.insight: This short verse packs immense theological depth in just a few words, demonstrating the miraculous eloquence of the Quran in conveying profound truths concisely.
gems.line: A handful of words holds a whole theology - the verse's brevity is itself Qur'anic eloquence.

lines.text: O God, You are my trust in every distress, and my hope in every hardship.
And when you have resolved, rely upon God. Indeed God loves those who rely.
Trust placed in Him, not in the outcome, cannot be broken by the outcome.

33:3.morning: One instruction covers everything on today's list: rely upon Allah - sufficient is He as Disposer of affairs.
33:3.night: The affairs you could not finish today have a Disposer - and sufficient is Allah as Wakil.

40:44.arabic: فَسَتَذْكُرُونَ مَآ أَقُولُ لَكُمْ ۚ وَأُفَوِّضُ أَمْرِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بَصِيرٌۢ بِٱلْعِبَادِ
40:44.translation: Soon you will remember what I tell you, and I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed Allah watches His servants.’

gems.title: You Will Remember
gems.insight: The believer prophetically tells them 'you will remember what I say to you' - truth eventually becomes undeniable, though often too late for those who rejected it.
gems.line: 'You will remember what I say' - truth outlasts its rejection, even when the rejecters learn late.

gems.title: Divine Entrustment
gems.insight: The believer entrusts his affair to Allah (ufawwidu amri ila Allah) - demonstrating complete reliance on divine protection after fulfilling the duty of warning.
gems.line: Ufawwidu amri ila Allah - the believer spoke it after his duty was done; entrustment follows effort.

gems.title: Divine Witness
gems.insight: Allah is 'Seeing of His servants' (basir bil-ibad) - complete divine awareness of every servant's situation, struggle, and sincerity provides ultimate accountability and comfort.
gems.line: Basir bil-ibad - your struggle and sincerity are fully seen, and that seeing is also comfort.

lines.text: O God, You are my trust in every distress, and my hope in every hardship.
And when you have resolved, rely upon God. Indeed God loves those who rely.
Trust placed in Him, not in the outcome, cannot be broken by the outcome.

40:44.morning: 'I entrust my affair to Allah' - words first said under threat, and they fit any day's uncertainty.
40:44.night: The believer's words close today well: I entrust my affair to Allah, and He is Seeing of His servants.

41:30.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوا۟ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَقَٰمُوا۟ تَتَنَزَّلُ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ أَلَّا تَخَافُوا۟ وَلَا تَحْزَنُوا۟ وَأَبْشِرُوا۟ بِٱلْجَنَّةِ ٱلَّتِى كُنتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ
41:30.translation: Indeed those who say, ‘Our Lord is Allah!’ and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them, [saying,] ‘Do not fear, nor be grieved! Receive the good news of the paradise, which you have been promised.

gems.title: Our Lord is Allah
gems.insight: Those who declared 'Our Lord is Allah' and then remained steadfast are promised angelic visitation with glad tidings.
gems.line: The declaration plus the staying - to those two together, angels bring glad tidings.

gems.title: Then Steadfast
gems.insight: The critical word is 'then remained steadfast' (istaqamu) - showing that initial belief must be followed by consistent righteous living.
gems.line: Thumma istaqamu - the 'then' matters; belief is the start, consistency is the evidence.

gems.title: Angels Descend
gems.insight: Angels will descend upon the steadfast believers at death, bringing comfort and reassurance in their most vulnerable moment.
gems.line: At the most vulnerable moment, angels descend on the steadfast - reassurance arrives right then.

gems.title: Triple Comfort
gems.insight: The angels say three things: 'Do not fear, do not grieve, and receive good tidings of Paradise' - addressing past, present, and future concerns.
gems.line: Do not fear, do not grieve, receive glad tidings - past, present, and future each answered.

lines.text: O God, You are my trust in every distress, and my hope in every hardship.
And when you have resolved, rely upon God. Indeed God loves those who rely.
Trust placed in Him, not in the outcome, cannot be broken by the outcome.

41:30.morning: 'Our Lord is Allah' is the declaration; today offers what the verse prizes next - remaining steady on it.
41:30.night: If today was one more day of holding to 'Our Lord is Allah,' the angels' three comforts stand ahead.

51:58.arabic: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلرَّزَّاقُ ذُو ٱلْقُوَّةِ ٱلْمَتِينُ
51:58.translation: Indeed it is Allah who is the All-provider, Powerful and All-strong.

gems.title: The Provider
gems.insight: Allah is 'Ar-Razzaq' (the continual Provider) - not just giving provision once, but constantly sustaining all creation with unfailing generosity.
gems.line: Ar-Razzaq provides continually - today's sustenance is a fresh giving, not a leftover.

gems.title: Firm Power
gems.insight: Allah possesses 'firm strength' (dhu al-quwwati al-matin) - His power is unshakeable, never weakening or requiring reinforcement.
gems.line: His strength is matin - firm, needing no reinforcement; what rests on it does not shake.

gems.title: The All-Strong
gems.insight: The attribute 'Al-Qawi' (The Strong) combined with 'Al-Matin' (The Firm) creates comprehensive strength - both powerful and unshakeable.
gems.line: Strong and firm together - power that carries joined to power that cannot be shaken.

gems.title: Divine Contrast
gems.insight: This verse contrasts sharply with the previous - humans need provision, Allah provides it; we require strength, He possesses it infinitely.
gems.line: You need provision and strength; He owns both without need - the dependence runs one way only.

lines.text: O God, You are my trust in every distress, and my hope in every hardship.
And when you have resolved, rely upon God. Indeed God loves those who rely.
Trust placed in Him, not in the outcome, cannot be broken by the outcome.

51:58.morning: Today's provision has a named source - Ar-Razzaq, the continual Provider, firm possessor of strength.
51:58.night: You did not sustain yourself today - Ar-Razzaq did, from strength that never once thinned.

64:11.arabic: مَآ أَصَابَ مِن مُّصِيبَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ ۗ وَمَن يُؤْمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُۥ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌۭ
64:11.translation: No affliction visits [anyone] except by Allah’s leave. Whoever has faith in Allah, He guides his heart, and Allah has knowledge of all things.

gems.title: By Allah's Leave
gems.insight: No disaster strikes except by Allah's permission (bi-idhn Allah) - nothing happens outside divine decree, providing comfort that chaos doesn't rule the universe.
gems.line: No disaster arrives at random - everything passes through His permission first; chaos does not rule.

gems.title: Heart Guidance
gems.insight: Whoever believes in Allah, 'He will guide his heart' (yahdi qalbahu) - faith opens the door to spiritual guidance and inner peace during trials.
gems.line: 'Whoever believes in Allah - He will guide his heart' - steadiness inside the trial is His gift.

gems.title: Allah Knows All
gems.insight: The verse concludes 'Allah is Knowing of all things' ('Alim bi-kulli shay') - His knowledge encompasses every aspect of our trials and their purposes.
gems.line: He knows every side of what tries you - including the purpose it is serving.

lines.text: O God, You are my trust in every distress, and my hope in every hardship.
And when you have resolved, rely upon God. Indeed God loves those who rely.
Trust placed in Him, not in the outcome, cannot be broken by the outcome.

64:11.morning: Nothing can strike today outside His permission - and the believing heart travels under His guidance.
64:11.night: Whatever today carried came by His leave - and the heart that believes is guided through it, not around it.

65:3.arabic: وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ ۚ وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُۥٓ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بَٰلِغُ أَمْرِهِۦ ۚ قَدْ جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدْرًۭا
65:3.translation: and provide for him from whence he does not count upon. And whoever puts his trust in Allah, He will suffice him. Indeed Allah carries through His commands. Certainly, Allah has ordained a measure [and extent] for everything.

gems.title: Unexpected Provision
gems.insight: Allah provides 'from where one does not expect' - sustenance comes through unimaginable channels when we maintain taqwa, especially during financial uncertainty like divorce.
gems.line: He provides from where you do not expect - your visible options are not His limits.

gems.title: Total Reliance
gems.insight: Tawakkul (reliance on Allah) means He becomes 'sufficient' - not just a helper, but enough. Those who trust Allah completely find Him to be all they need.
gems.line: 'He is sufficient for him' - not a helper alongside your plans, but enough by Himself.

gems.title: Measured Decree
gems.insight: Allah has set a 'qadr' (precise measure) for everything - every difficulty has a predetermined limit and duration. Nothing is random or eternal except by His will.
gems.line: Every difficulty has a set measure - what you carry now has a limit already decreed.

gems.title: Divine Purpose
gems.insight: Allah is 'baligh amrihi' - He accomplishes His purpose. Every divine command reaches its intended goal with perfect precision.
gems.line: Allah accomplishes His purpose - whatever stands between, His command reaches its goal.

lines.text: O God, You are my trust in every distress, and my hope in every hardship.
And when you have resolved, rely upon God. Indeed God loves those who rely.
Trust placed in Him, not in the outcome, cannot be broken by the outcome.

65:3.morning: Provision can reach you today from a direction you never planned - He is enough for whoever relies on Him.
65:3.night: Rest on the verse's two footholds - He suffices the one who relies, and all things are held to His measure.

73:9.arabic: رَّبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ وَٱلْمَغْرِبِ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَٱتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلًۭا
73:9.translation: Lord of the east and the west, there is no god except Him; so take Him for your trustee,

gems.title: Universal Sovereignty
gems.insight: 'Lord of the East and West' affirms Allah's absolute sovereignty over all creation, all directions, all realms - nothing exists outside His domain.
gems.line: East, west, and everything between belong to Him - nothing you cross today lies outside His domain.

gems.title: Pure Monotheism
gems.insight: 'There is no deity except Him' (la ilaha illa huwa) is Islam's central creed - absolute tawhid rejecting all forms of shirk and false worship.
gems.line: 'There is no deity except Him' - the creed stands whole, leaving no rival claim on your reliance.

gems.title: Ultimate Reliance
gems.insight: 'Take Him as Disposer of affairs' (fattakhidhu wakeela) means entrusting all matters to Allah, relying on His management rather than our limited understanding.
gems.line: A wakil is trusted with what you hand over - the verse invites you to hand your affairs to Him.

lines.text: O God, You are my trust in every distress, and my hope in every hardship.
And when you have resolved, rely upon God. Indeed God loves those who rely.
Trust placed in Him, not in the outcome, cannot be broken by the outcome.

73:9.morning: Lord of the east and the west - wherever today moves, take Him as the keeper of your affairs.
73:9.night: What is unfinished tonight has a Disposer - leave your affairs with the Lord of the east and the west.

2:37.arabic: فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتٍۢ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:37.translation: Then Adam received certain words from his Lord, and He turned to him clemently. Indeed He is the All-clement, the All-merciful.

gems.title: Divine Words
gems.insight: Adam received specific words from Allah that enabled his repentance. According to Shia traditions, these words included the names of Muhammad and the Ahlul Bayt.
gems.line: Adam's way back was carried by names: Muhammad and his family, taught to him by his Lord.

gems.title: Accepting Repentance
gems.insight: Allah accepted Adam's repentance after he used the divinely taught words. This established the principle that sincere repentance is always accepted.
gems.line: Adam's repentance was accepted - and with it the rule was set: sincere return is always received.

gems.title: The Ever-Accepting
gems.insight: Al-Tawwab means the One who repeatedly accepts repentance. Combined with Al-Rahim, it shows Allah's nature is to forgive and show mercy.
gems.line: He is al-Tawwab: the One who accepts return after return. Coming back twice is not too many times.

gems.title: From His Lord
gems.insight: The phrase 'from his Lord' emphasizes that guidance for repentance comes from Allah, not human invention. Adam needed divine assistance.
gems.line: Even the words of return came from his Lord. The urge to turn back is itself His assistance.

lines.text: I have submitted to the Lord of all the worlds.
The cow God asked for was free; the cow their questions built cost its weight in gold.
Obedience was always the shortest road; only our questions ever made it long.

2:37.morning: Adam's story starts over with words his Lord gave him. Whatever yesterday held, today can begin again.
2:37.night: If anything today needs undoing, the One who taught Adam how to return is still al-Tawwab tonight.

3:133.arabic: ۞ وَسَارِعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُهَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلْأَرْضُ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ
3:133.translation: Hasten towards your Lord’s forgiveness and a paradise as vast as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the Godwary

gems.title: Hasten to Forgiveness
gems.insight: The command 'hasten' (sari'u) implies urgency and competition in seeking Allah's forgiveness - treating it as a race to be won, not a casual stroll.
gems.line: Sari'u - hasten. Forgiveness is approached at a run, not saved for some quieter season.

gems.title: Paradise's Vastness
gems.insight: Paradise's width is 'as wide as the heavens and earth' - a metaphor for unimaginable expanse, beauty, and generosity beyond human comprehension.
gems.line: What is prepared spans the heavens and the earth - generosity too wide for the mind to fence in.

gems.title: For the Righteous
gems.insight: Paradise is 'prepared for the muttaqin' (righteous/God-conscious) - those who embody taqwa through action, not just claim it verbally.
gems.line: Paradise stands prepared for the people of taqwa - the ones who live it, not just say it.

gems.title: Spiritual Race
gems.insight: The verse uses competitive language - hastening, racing toward forgiveness and Paradise - framing spirituality as active pursuit, not passive reception.
gems.line: Faith here moves like a race - forgiveness and Paradise are pursued, not passively awaited.

lines.text: When the truth was put on trial, God reached not for a sword but for a purified family.
One word - purified - travels from Maryam's prayer-niche to the five beneath the cloak.

3:133.morning: Forgiveness is not waiting for you to wander over - the verse says hasten, and today is ground to cover.
3:133.night: However far you moved toward His forgiveness today, it counts as racing - and the garden is prepared.

4:27.arabic: وَٱللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَن يَتُوبَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَيُرِيدُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلشَّهَوَٰتِ أَن تَمِيلُوا۟ مَيْلًا عَظِيمًۭا
4:27.translation: Allah desires to turn toward you clemently, but those who pursue their [base] appetites desire that you fall into gross waywardness.

gems.title: Merciful Intent
gems.insight: Allah's primary desire is to accept our repentance and guide us toward righteousness and spiritual growth.
gems.line: His first wish for you is stated outright: to accept your repentance and turn you toward growth.

gems.title: Opposing Forces
gems.insight: Those enslaved by their passions actively want believers to deviate greatly from the straight path.
gems.line: Not every voice wants your steadiness - those led by their passions prefer company in the drift.

gems.title: Severe Warning
gems.insight: The phrase 'great deviation' emphasizes that following desires leads not to minor mistakes but to major spiritual loss.
gems.line: The deviation desired for you is called great - drifting with appetite is rarely a small detour.

lines.text: Taste this, Ali - taste the fire. This is for the one who fails the widow and the orphan.
A right on a page protects no one; every right is a trust placed in someone's hands.
Obedience closes the distance that love alone cannot close.

4:27.morning: Allah wants to accept your return - that intention stands over today, whatever pulls the other way.
4:27.night: However today wavered, His wish tonight is unchanged: He wants to accept your return.

4:106.arabic: وَٱسْتَغْفِرِ ٱللَّهَ ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورًۭا رَّحِيمًۭا
4:106.translation: and plead to Allah for forgiveness; indeed Allah is all-forgiving, all-merciful.

gems.title: Seeking Forgiveness
gems.insight: The command to seek Allah's forgiveness emphasizes repentance as a continuous spiritual practice, not just a one-time act. Allah's names Al-Ghafoor and Ar-Raheem assure us that His mercy always surpasses His judgment.
gems.line: Repentance is a practice, not an emergency exit - and His mercy outweighs His judgment.

gems.title: Divine Mercy
gems.insight: The verse concludes with two of Allah's beautiful names - Al-Ghafoor (The Most Forgiving) and Ar-Raheem (The Most Merciful). These aren't temporary states but eternal attributes, emphasizing that forgiveness is central to Allah's relationship with humanity.
gems.line: Ghafoor and Raheem are not passing moods - forgiving is who He eternally is.

gems.title: Continuous Repentance
gems.insight: The imperative form of 'seek forgiveness' indicates that repentance should be an ongoing practice, not reserved for major sins. The Prophet would seek forgiveness 70-100 times daily, teaching us that spiritual purification is continuous.
gems.line: The Prophet sought forgiveness many times a day - asking often is the practice, not the failure.

lines.text: Taste this, Ali - taste the fire. This is for the one who fails the widow and the orphan.
A right on a page protects no one; every right is a trust placed in someone's hands.
Obedience closes the distance that love alone cannot close.

4:106.morning: Seeking forgiveness is not a yearly event - it belongs inside an ordinary day like this one.
4:106.night: The verse's instruction fits the end of a day: seek His forgiveness - He is ever Forgiving, Merciful.

5:39.arabic: فَمَن تَابَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ ظُلْمِهِۦ وَأَصْلَحَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌ
5:39.translation: But whoever repents after his wrongdoing, and reforms, then Allah shall accept his repentance. Indeed Allah is all-forgiving, all-merciful.

gems.title: Repentance & Reform
gems.insight: Even after committing theft, sincere repentance (tawba) combined with reform (islah) opens the door to Allah's forgiveness.
gems.line: No wrong is past the reach of tawba - sincere return with real repair reopens the door.

gems.title: Reform Requirement
gems.insight: True repentance isn't just regret; it requires 'islah' (reform) - actively correcting behavior and making amends.
gems.line: Regret alone is half of repentance - islah, actually setting things right, completes it.

gems.title: Divine Acceptance
gems.insight: Allah's turning to the repentant in forgiveness ('yatub alayhi') shows active divine response to human transformation.
gems.line: When you turn back, He responds by turning to you - repentance is met, not merely permitted.

lines.text: He whose mawla I am - whose guardian and master I am - this Ali is his mawla.
This day I have perfected for you your religion, and completed My favor upon you...
You renew the oldest pledge every time you stand to pray: we hear, and we obey.

5:39.morning: Yesterday's wrong does not get the last word - repentance joined to repair opens His turning to you.
5:39.night: If you turned back and set something right today, His answer is already in the verse: He turns to you.

7:23.arabic: قَالَا رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَآ أَنفُسَنَا وَإِن لَّمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ
7:23.translation: They said, ‘Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves! If You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers.’

gems.title: Model Repentance
gems.insight: Adam and his wife's repentance contains three elements: admission of wrong ('we have wronged ourselves'), seeking forgiveness, and requesting mercy - the perfect template for sincere tawbah.
gems.line: Adam's prayer is the template: admit the wrong, ask forgiveness, ask for mercy - in that order.

gems.title: Wronging Ourselves
gems.insight: They say 'we have wronged ourselves' (zalamna anfusana), not 'we have wronged You, Allah' - recognizing that sin primarily harms the sinner, not God.
gems.line: 'We have wronged ourselves' - sin's first casualty is your own soul, and honest return says so.

gems.title: Complete Dependence
gems.insight: The phrase 'if You do not forgive us...we will surely be among the losers' shows complete awareness that salvation depends entirely on Allah's mercy, not our deeds.
gems.line: Even Adam did not lean on his record - 'if You do not forgive us' rests everything on His mercy.

gems.title: Contrasting Responses
gems.insight: Unlike Satan who blamed Allah and persisted in defiance, Adam and his wife immediately repented with humility - showing that our response to sin determines our destiny.
gems.line: Satan blamed and persisted; Adam and his wife turned back at once - the response decided everything.

lines.text: You said yes once, before you can remember; your life is the second time you are asked.
They walked in as Pharaoh's hired magicians at sunrise; before sunset they were martyrs.
Pride, heedlessness, or a slow letting-go: every fall in al-A'raf is one promise slipping.

7:23.morning: Whatever yesterday held, Adam's words are yours this morning: our Lord, we have wronged ourselves.
7:23.night: Adam's words fit the close of a day: we have wronged ourselves - forgive us, have mercy, or we are lost.

9:104.arabic: أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ يَقْبَلُ ٱلتَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَأْخُذُ ٱلصَّدَقَٰتِ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
9:104.translation: Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts the repentance of His servants and receives the charities, and that it is Allah who is the All-clement, the All-merciful?

gems.title: Allah Accepts Tawbah
gems.insight: 'Do they not know that Allah accepts repentance from His servants?' - emphasizing that sincere tawbah is always accepted, no matter the sin.
gems.line: Sincere tawba is never left pending - no matter the sin, acceptance is already His stated way.

gems.title: Receives Charities
gems.insight: 'And receives charities' (ya'khudh as-sadaqat) - Allah Himself receives our charity, elevating the act beyond mere human transaction to divine encounter.
gems.line: Charity never stops at the receiving hand - He Himself takes it. Giving today is divine encounter.

gems.title: Oft-Returning, Merciful
gems.insight: 'Allah is the Accepting of repentance (At-Tawwab), the Merciful (Ar-Raheem)' - His names emphasize that He repeatedly accepts those who repeatedly return to Him.
gems.line: At-Tawwab accepts those who return again and again - repeat returns are what His name promises.

lines.text: Before you ever turned toward God, He had already turned toward you.
The one who repents of a sin is as one with no sin at all.
Every road away from God turns, and leads back into His mercy.

9:104.morning: Today opens on a settled fact: it is Allah Himself who accepts repentance from His servants.
9:104.night: If tonight holds regret, the verse has answered in advance: He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.

11:61.arabic: ۞ وَإِلَىٰ ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمْ صَٰلِحًۭا ۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥ ۖ هُوَ أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱسْتَعْمَرَكُمْ فِيهَا فَٱسْتَغْفِرُوهُ ثُمَّ تُوبُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِ ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّى قَرِيبٌۭ مُّجِيبٌۭ
11:61.translation: And to Thamud [We sent] Salih, their brother. He said, ‘O my people! Worship Allah. You have no other god besides Him. He brought you forth from the earth and made it your habitation. So plead with Him for forgiveness, then turn to Him penitently. My Lord is indeed nearmost [and] responsive.’

gems.title: Brother's Call
gems.insight: Salih is called 'their brother' (أَخَاهُمْ), emphasizing prophets come from within communities, not as alien outsiders. This linguistic choice shows divine mercy - Allah sends guides who understand their people's language, culture, and struggles intimately.
gems.line: Salih came as 'their brother' - Allah guides through those who know your language and struggles.

gems.title: Pure Monotheism
gems.insight: The core message 'worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him' (ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥ) is the universal call of all prophets. This uncompromising monotheism rejects all forms of shirk, whether idol worship or submission to worldly powers.
gems.line: Beneath every prophet's message runs one call: worship Allah alone - nothing else merits submission.

gems.title: Divine Stewardship
gems.insight: Allah 'produced you from the earth and settled you in it' (أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱسْتَعْمَرَكُمْ فِيهَا). The word ista'marakum implies being appointed as custodians - humans are trustees of Earth, responsible for its development and care.
gems.line: Raised from this earth and settled in it as its custodian - the ground you walk is a trust.

gems.title: Near and Responsive
gems.insight: Salih concludes with divine attributes: 'my Lord is near and responsive' (إِنَّ رَبِّى قَرِيبٌۭ مُّجِيبٌۭ). Qarib (near) speaks to Allah's intimate proximity, while Mujib (responsive) assures that sincere repentance never goes unheard.
gems.line: Qarib and Mujib - near, and answering. A sincere return never has to shout to be heard.

lines.text: Hud and its sisters have grayed me.
The same surah that grayed the Prophet was built, story by story, to steady his heart.
Fear needs a second power. Hud counted the powers in the world and came to one.

11:61.morning: Salih's assurance to his people opens your day as well: my Lord is near and responsive.
11:61.night: Salih's words hold at the day's end: ask His forgiveness, turn to Him - your Lord is near and answers.

12:53.arabic: ۞ وَمَآ أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِىٓ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلنَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌۢ بِٱلسُّوٓءِ إِلَّا مَا رَحِمَ رَبِّىٓ ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّى غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
12:53.translation: ‘Yet I do not absolve my [own carnal] soul, for the [carnal] soul indeed prompts [men] to evil, except inasmuch as my Lord has mercy. Indeed my Lord is all-forgiving, all-merciful.’

gems.title: Self-Awareness
gems.insight: 'I do not acquit myself' - despite being vindicated, Yusuf acknowledges human vulnerability to sin. Even prophets recognize their dependence on divine mercy.
gems.line: Even cleared of blame, Yusuf claimed no innocence - honesty about the self is prophetic practice.

gems.title: Soul's Battle
gems.insight: 'The soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil' - the nafs constantly inclines toward wrong unless controlled by faith. Spiritual growth is an ongoing struggle, not a destination.
gems.line: The nafs keeps urging wrong - the struggle you feel is not failure; it is the standing condition.

gems.title: Mercy's Exception
gems.insight: 'Except those upon which my Lord has mercy' - only Allah's mercy protects us from our own evil inclinations. Success in resisting sin is divine grace, not personal achievement.
gems.line: Every resisted sin was His mercy at work - restraint is grace received, not strength self-made.

gems.title: Allah's Nature
gems.insight: 'Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful' - concluding with divine attributes emphasizes that despite our weakness, Allah's forgiveness and mercy are always available.
gems.line: The verse ends where weakness needs it to: my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful - always within reach.

lines.text: No blame upon you today. May God forgive you, and He is the most merciful of the merciful.
Beautiful patience is the certainty that God keeps an account no darkness can erase.
Every pit was a road; from the well to the throne, not one hour was wasted.

12:53.morning: Yusuf, though vindicated, would not acquit his own soul - watchfulness over the nafs is today's work too.
12:53.night: The soul urged today; sometimes you resisted. Both truths end in one place: my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful.

12:92.arabic: قَالَ لَا تَثْرِيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ ۖ يَغْفِرُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ ۖ وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
12:92.translation: He said, ‘There shall be no reproach on you today. Allah will forgive you, and He is the most merciful of the merciful.

gems.title: No Reproach
gems.insight: Yusuf echoes the Prophet Yusuf's (as) words in forgiving his brothers without reproach. This noble response mirrors Prophet Muhammad's (saw) forgiveness of Makkans, showing that true nobility lies in pardoning those who wrong us.
gems.line: Yusuf pardoned without reproach - the same nobility the Prophet later showed the people of Makkah.

gems.title: Allah's Forgiveness
gems.insight: Yusuf directs his brothers to Allah's forgiveness, acknowledging that only Allah can truly forgive sins. Human forgiveness removes worldly consequences, but divine forgiveness purifies the soul.
gems.line: Yusuf forgave, then pointed to Allah - human pardon settles accounts; His forgiveness purifies.

gems.title: Most Merciful
gems.insight: The title 'Most Merciful of the merciful' (Arham al-Rahimeen) emphasizes that Allah's mercy surpasses all human mercy. Even Yusuf's extraordinary forgiveness pales before Allah's infinite compassion.
gems.line: Arham al-Rahimin, most merciful of the merciful - even Yusuf's pardon runs small beside His.

lines.text: No blame upon you today. May God forgive you, and He is the most merciful of the merciful.
Beautiful patience is the certainty that God keeps an account no darkness can erase.
Every pit was a road; from the well to the throne, not one hour was wasted.

12:92.morning: Yusuf faced the brothers who wronged him and chose: no blame today. Forgiveness that complete exists.
12:92.night: Yusuf's 'no blame upon you today' drew on a deeper well - He is the most merciful of the merciful.

14:41.arabic: رَبَّنَا ٱغْفِرْ لِى وَلِوَٰلِدَىَّ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلْحِسَابُ
14:41.translation: Our Lord! Forgive me and my parents, and all the faithful, on the day when the reckoning is held.’

gems.title: Parental Forgiveness
gems.insight: Ibrahim prayed for his parents' forgiveness - honoring them and hoping for their guidance even while upholding pure monotheism.
gems.line: Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his parents - honoring them while holding fast to pure monotheism.

gems.title: Ummah's Forgiveness
gems.insight: Ibrahim extended his prayer to all believers - showing prophets care for the entire community, not just themselves.
gems.line: His prayer stretched to all believers - a heart formed by prophethood asks for everyone.

gems.title: Judgment Day
gems.insight: The Day the account is established - when all deeds are weighed, all secrets revealed, and eternal fate decided.
gems.line: The prayer aims at the Day the account stands - forgiveness matters most where deeds are weighed.

lines.text: A good word is like a good tree: its root is firm, and its branch reaches into the sky.
I am the prayer of my father Ibrahim.
What is planted with God in dead ground is never wasted; it grows while you are gone.

14:41.morning: Ibrahim's circle of forgiveness took in his parents and every believer - yours can open that wide today.
14:41.night: Ibrahim's prayer fits tonight as it is: forgive me, my parents, and the believers, on the Day of account.

17:25.arabic: رَّبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا فِى نُفُوسِكُمْ ۚ إِن تَكُونُوا۟ صَٰلِحِينَ فَإِنَّهُۥ كَانَ لِلْأَوَّٰبِينَ غَفُورًۭا
17:25.translation: Your Lord knows best what is in your hearts. Should you be righteous, He is indeed most forgiving toward penitents.

gems.title: Inner Secrets
gems.insight: Allah declares 'Your Lord is most knowing of what is within yourselves' (رَّبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا فِى نُفُوسِكُمْ). While we may outwardly comply with parental duties, Allah sees our true intentions - whether we serve from love or mere obligation.
gems.line: Outward duty can be seen by anyone - the love or reluctance beneath it is read by your Lord alone.

gems.title: Repentance Path
gems.insight: The verse promises 'if you should be righteous, He is ever Forgiving to the oft-returning' (إِن تَكُونُوا۟ صَٰلِحِينَ فَإِنَّهُۥ كَانَ لِلْأَوَّٰبِينَ غَفُورًۭا). Past failures with parents can be forgiven if we genuinely repent and become among the awwabeen - those who constantly turn back to Allah.
gems.line: Past failures with parents are not final - genuine return finds Him ever-Forgiving.

gems.title: Constant Returners
gems.insight: The term awwabeen (ٱلْأَوَّٰبِينَ) refers to those who habitually return to Allah after slipping. This isn't one-time repentance but a lifestyle of recognizing mistakes, seeking forgiveness, and striving to improve - especially in parental relations.
gems.line: Awwabin keep coming back after slipping - a lifetime of returning, and He receives every return.

gems.title: Righteous Living
gems.insight: The condition 'if you should be righteous' (إِن تَكُونُوا۟ صَٰلِحِينَ) links forgiveness for parental shortcomings to overall righteous character. We can't claim repentance while persisting in other sins; comprehensive reform demonstrates sincerity.
gems.line: Sincerity shows across a whole life - righteous character is what carries the repentance.

17:25.morning: Your Lord reads what is within you - the intention beneath today's duties is fully seen.
17:25.night: Whatever fell short today, the verse answered ahead - to those who keep returning, He is Forgiving.

21:87.arabic: وَذَا ٱلنُّونِ إِذ ذَّهَبَ مُغَٰضِبًۭا فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ فَنَادَىٰ فِى ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ أَن لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
21:87.translation: And [remember] the Man of the Fish, when he left in a rage, thinking that We would not put him to hardship. Then he cried out in the darkness, ‘There is no god except You! You are immaculate! I have indeed been among the wrongdoers!’

gems.title: The Fish's Companion
gems.insight: Jonah is called 'dha al-noon' (the man of the fish/whale), forever identified with his trial in the belly of the whale—a reminder that prophets face unique, defining tests.
gems.line: The Qur'an names Yunus by his trial - even prophets carry one defining test through their story.

gems.title: Prophetic Emotion
gems.insight: Jonah 'went off in anger' (dhahaba mughadiban) from his people—even prophets experience human emotions like frustration when their message is rejected.
gems.line: Yunus left in anger at rejection - frustration is human, felt even by prophets carrying truth.

gems.title: Temporary Doubt
gems.insight: Jonah 'thought that We would not decree anything upon him' (dhanna an lan naqdira 'alayhi)—a momentary lapse where he thought he could escape his prophetic duty.
gems.line: For a moment he thought distance was possible - a lapse the Qur'an records without hiding it.

gems.title: Prayer in Darkness
gems.insight: Jonah called out 'in the darknesses' (fi al-dhulumat)—the darkness of the night, the sea, and the whale's belly, representing physical and spiritual crisis.
gems.line: 'In the darknesses' - night, sea, and the whale's belly - crisis layered three deep, and he prayed.

21:87.morning: From night, sea, and the whale's belly, Yunus still called - no darkness today is too deep to pray from.
21:87.night: The words from the darknesses fit this hour: no deity but You, glory to You, I was of the wrongdoers.

23:118.arabic: وَقُل رَّبِّ ٱغْفِرْ وَٱرْحَمْ وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
23:118.translation: Say, ‘My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and You are the best of the merciful.’

gems.title: Prophet's Supplication
gems.insight: Allah commands the Prophet (ﷺ) to say 'My Lord, forgive and have mercy' - teaching us the proper way to seek Allah's grace through combining requests for forgiveness and mercy.
gems.line: The wording was given to the Prophet - making it the taught, reliable way to ask for grace.

gems.title: Dual Request
gems.insight: Asking for both 'forgiveness' (maghfirah - covering sins) and 'mercy' (rahmah - positive grace) shows we need Allah to both remove our faults and grant us His blessings.
gems.line: Forgiveness covers what you did; mercy adds what you lack - the prayer asks for both at once.

gems.title: Supreme Mercy
gems.insight: 'You are the Best of the Merciful' echoes verse 109, bookending the section by affirming that Allah's mercy surpasses all other mercy.
gems.line: 'Best of the merciful' - every other mercy you have ever received stands below His.

gems.title: Surah's Finale
gems.insight: This verse perfectly concludes Surah al-Mu'minun, which began describing believers' qualities and ends with a prayer embodying those qualities - humility, hope in Allah's mercy, and complete reliance on Him.
gems.line: A surah describing believers ends in this plea - humility and hope are where its qualities arrive.

23:118.morning: The Prophet was taught the day's shortest prayer: 'My Lord, forgive and have mercy' - and it is yours to say.
23:118.night: The surah's last words fit the day's last hour: My Lord, forgive and have mercy, best of the merciful.

25:71.arabic: وَمَن تَابَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا فَإِنَّهُۥ يَتُوبُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَتَابًۭا
25:71.translation: And whoever repents and acts righteously indeed turns to Allah with due penitence).

gems.title: Accepted Return
gems.insight: Whoever repents and does righteousness 'turns to Allah with accepted repentance' (yatubu ila Allah mataba) - emphasizing the completeness of return.
gems.line: Tawba joined to changed deeds is described as arriving - a return to Allah that is received.

gems.title: Deeds Matter
gems.insight: Repentance alone isn't enough; it must be accompanied by 'righteous work' (amal salihan) - change requires both internal and external transformation.
gems.line: Regret alone is half the turn - the verse asks the inside and the outside to change together.

gems.title: Complete Turning
gems.insight: The word 'mataban' (absolute verbal noun) emphasizes totality - this is not partial or half-hearted, but complete and wholehearted return to Allah.
gems.line: Mataba - the wording is total: not a half-turn or a hedge, but a whole return to Allah.

25:71.morning: Turning back to Him is open this morning - and the verse pairs it with right action to make it whole.
25:71.night: If today held one honest turning and one right deed, the verse calls that a true return to Him.

28:67.arabic: فَأَمَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا فَعَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُفْلِحِينَ
28:67.translation: As for him who repents, has faith and acts righteously, maybe he will be among the felicitous.

gems.title: Path of Hope
gems.insight: After describing punishment, Allah offers hope: 'But as for one who repented, believed, and did righteousness' - the door to salvation remains open.
gems.line: This verse follows warning on purpose - however dark the description, the way back stays open.

gems.title: Three Conditions
gems.insight: Success requires three integrated elements: tawba (repentance), iman (faith), and 'amal salih (righteous deeds) - heart, belief, and action together.
gems.line: Success asks for three together: a turning heart, a believing conviction, and hands that do right.

gems.title: Among Successful
gems.insight: The phrase 'fa'asa an yakun min al-muflihun' uses 'asa (it is hoped/expected) - expressing divine mercy and the promise of success for those who fulfill the conditions.
gems.line: When Allah says 'it is hoped', mercy is speaking - for the one who returns, the outcome is success.

28:67.morning: The door out of any past stands open today: repent, believe, do right - and success is the promised end.
28:67.night: If any part of today was a turning back to Him, you end it among those this verse expects to succeed.

42:25.arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى يَقْبَلُ ٱلتَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَعْفُوا۟ عَنِ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ
42:25.translation: It is He who accepts the repentance of His servants, and excuses their misdeeds and knows what you do.

gems.title: Accepting Repentance
gems.insight: Allah accepts repentance (tawbah) from His servants, showing that the door to forgiveness is always open regardless of past sins, as long as we sincerely turn back.
gems.line: No past disqualifies a sincere return - tawba's door stands open to every servant who turns back.

gems.title: Pardoning Sins
gems.insight: Allah pardons misdeeds (ya'fu 'an al-sayyi'at), not just accepting repentance but actively erasing sins and their consequences through divine mercy.
gems.line: Pardon here is active - misdeeds and their traces erased by mercy, not merely overlooked.

gems.title: Knowing Actions
gems.insight: Allah knows what we do (ya'lamu ma taf'alun) - complete awareness of all our actions, both those we hide and those we reveal, making accountability comprehensive.
gems.line: He knows what you do - hidden and shown alike; nothing sits outside the accounting.

42:25.morning: Today runs under an open door - He accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds.
42:25.night: He saw all of today - and the same verse that says He knows says He accepts and He pardons.

47:19.arabic: فَٱعْلَمْ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْ لِذَنۢبِكَ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مُتَقَلَّبَكُمْ وَمَثْوَىٰكُمْ
47:19.translation: Know that there is no god except Allah, and plead [to Allah] for forgiveness of your sin and for the faithful, men and women. Allah knows your itinerary and your [final] abode.

gems.title: Foundational Knowledge
gems.insight: 'Fa'lam' (فَٱعْلَمْ) means 'know with certainty'—not belief or opinion, but absolute conviction that there is no deity except Allah. This is the foundation of all Islamic spirituality.
gems.line: Fa'lam - know it beyond opinion or inheritance: no deity except Allah, as settled certainty.

gems.title: Prophetic Humility
gems.insight: Even Prophet Muhammad is commanded to seek forgiveness—this isn't admission of sin but demonstration of ultimate servitude and acknowledgment that perfection belongs to Allah alone.
gems.line: Even the Prophet was told to seek forgiveness - servitude at the summit, not admission of sin.

gems.title: Communal Care
gems.insight: The Prophet is commanded to seek forgiveness not just for himself but for all believers—establishing that spiritual leaders carry responsibility for their community's salvation.
gems.line: The Prophet was told to seek pardon for all believers - leadership carries its community's care.

gems.title: Complete Awareness
gems.insight: Allah knows your every movement and resting place—complete surveillance that should inspire both accountability and comfort, knowing nothing escapes divine attention.
gems.line: He knows your movement and your resting place - awareness that comforts as it calls to account.

47:19.morning: The day's first knowledge is its greatest - no deity except Allah, held as certainty, not habit.
47:19.night: You rest tonight inside the verse's last clause - your resting place known, the believers prayed for.

66:8.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ تُوبُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ تَوْبَةًۭ نَّصُوحًا عَسَىٰ رَبُّكُمْ أَن يُكَفِّرَ عَنكُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمْ وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ جَنَّٰتٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ يَوْمَ لَا يُخْزِى ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّبِىَّ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَعَهُۥ ۖ نُورُهُمْ يَسْعَىٰ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمَٰنِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا وَٱغْفِرْ لَنَآ ۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدِيرٌۭ
66:8.translation: O you who have faith! Repent to Allah with sincere repentance! Maybe your Lord will absolve you of your misdeeds and admit you into gardens with streams running in them, on the day when Allah will not let down the Prophet and the faithful who are with him. Their light will move swiftly before them and on their right. They will say, ‘Our Lord! Perfect our light for us, and forgive us! Indeed You have power over all things.’

gems.title: Sincere Tawbah
gems.insight: The term 'tawbatan nasuha' (sincere repentance) means complete, genuine return to Allah with regret for past sins and firm resolve never to return to them.
gems.line: Sincere repentance has two halves - real regret for what passed, firm resolve not to return to it.

gems.title: Hope for Forgiveness
gems.insight: Allah uses 'perhaps' (asa) when promising forgiveness, not from uncertainty but to encourage continuous striving and prevent complacency in repentance.
gems.line: 'Perhaps your Lord will remove your misdeeds' - the 'perhaps' keeps you striving, not presuming.

gems.title: Gardens of Paradise
gems.insight: The reward for sincere repentance is gardens 'beneath which rivers flow' - a vivid image of eternal bliss and spiritual refreshment in the Hereafter.
gems.line: For the sincerely returning, the verse holds out gardens with rivers flowing beneath.

gems.title: Light of Faith
gems.insight: Believers' light will 'proceed before them and on their right' on Judgment Day, symbolizing the guidance of faith illuminating their path to Paradise.
gems.line: That Day the Prophet and those who believed with him are not disgraced - their light runs out ahead.

66:8.morning: The day opens with an invitation to tawbatan nasuha - a sincere return that means not to go back.
66:8.night: Close the day with sincere return - and their prayer: 'Our Lord, perfect our light and forgive us.'

110:3.arabic: فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ تَوَّابًۢا
110:3.translation: celebrate the praise of your Lord, and plead to Him for forgiveness. Indeed, He is all-clement.

gems.title: Glorify with Praise
gems.insight: Tasbih (glorification) combined with hamd (praise) - declaring Allah's perfection while thanking Him - is the proper response to success, keeping us grounded in humility.
gems.line: The response to success is set - glorify and praise Him, and humility keeps its ground.

gems.title: Seek Forgiveness
gems.insight: Even in victory, seek istighfar (forgiveness) - acknowledging that perfection belongs to Allah alone and that even our best efforts contain shortcomings needing His mercy.
gems.line: Istighfar belongs even to victory - the best day's work still leans on His covering mercy.

gems.title: Ever-Accepting
gems.insight: Allah is 'Tawwab' - continuously accepting repentance, not just once but repeatedly. This divine attribute offers infinite opportunities for renewal and spiritual growth.
gems.line: Tawwab is a repeated acceptance - the door of return does not close after one use.

gems.title: Your Lord
gems.insight: The use of 'Rabbik' (your Lord) emphasizes the personal relationship between the Prophet and Allah - a Lord who nurtures, guides, and sustains His servant through all phases.
gems.line: 'Your Lord' - through every phase, the Prophet was nurtured, guided, and sustained personally.

110:3.morning: Should today succeed, the response is already written: exalt Him with praise, and ask His forgiveness.
110:3.night: End the day the way the Qur'an ends victories - praise, then istighfar, before the Ever-Accepting.

1:5.translation: You [alone] do we worship, and to You [alone] do we turn for help.

gems.title: Exclusive Worship
gems.insight: 'You alone we worship' - the emphatic structure in Arabic places Allah first, making worship exclusively His right.
gems.line: The verse says 'You alone' before 'we worship' - He comes first even in the grammar of your day.

gems.title: Seeking Help
gems.insight: 'You alone we ask for help' acknowledges our complete dependence on Allah for everything - guidance, strength, provision.
gems.line: Guidance, strength, provision - every kind of help you will need today has one source.

gems.title: Divine Dialogue
gems.insight: Here the surah shifts from third person (He) to second person (You) - moving from describing Allah to directly addressing Him in intimate conversation.
gems.line: Halfway through the Fatiha, talk about God becomes talk to Him. Prayer is that close.

lines.text: This is between Me and My servant - and My servant shall have what he asked.
The prayer God taught you to pray, He answers: the asking and the giving are one motion.
Al-Fatiha ends with a plea, guide us - and the very next page of the Qur'an is the answer.

1:5.morning: The day ahead rests on two anchors: worship that is His alone, and help that is His to give.
1:5.night: The day is done. Every bit of help that carried you through it came from the One you worship.

2:186.arabic: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِى عَنِّى فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ ۖ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا۟ لِى وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِى لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ
2:186.translation: When My servants ask you about Me, [tell them that] I am indeed nearmost. I answer the supplicant’s call when he calls Me. So let them respond to Me, and let them have faith in Me, so that they may fare rightly.

gems.title: Divine Nearness
gems.insight: Allah declares 'I am near' without intermediaries, establishing direct intimacy between Creator and servant. This nearness is not spatial but spiritual, transcending all barriers.
gems.line: No intermediary stands between you and Him - 'I am near' was said directly, to be taken directly.

gems.title: Answered Invocation
gems.insight: Allah promises to respond to every caller's invocation, establishing dua as a guaranteed dialogue rather than uncertain petition. The response is certain, though its form and timing belong to Divine wisdom.
gems.line: No call to Him goes unanswered - though the shape and hour of the answer rest with His wisdom.

gems.title: Mutual Response
gems.insight: The verse creates reciprocity: Allah responds to our calls, and we must respond to His commands through obedience and faith. Divine-human relationship is bidirectional.
gems.line: He answers when you call; the verse asks you to answer when He calls. The line runs both ways.

gems.title: Right Guidance
gems.insight: The verse connects prayer, obedience, and faith to rushd (right guidance), showing that spiritual maturity emerges from this threefold practice.
gems.line: Prayer, obedience, and faith travel together - and right guidance is where they arrive.

lines.text: I have submitted to the Lord of all the worlds.
The cow God asked for was free; the cow their questions built cost its weight in gold.
Obedience was always the shortest road; only our questions ever made it long.

2:186.morning: Before you ask anything today, the answer to the question of where He is has already come: near.
2:186.night: Whatever you whispered to Him today did not have far to travel. He was near the whole time.

3:38.arabic: هُنَالِكَ دَعَا زَكَرِيَّا رَبَّهُۥ ۖ قَالَ رَبِّ هَبْ لِى مِن لَّدُنكَ ذُرِّيَّةًۭ طَيِّبَةً ۖ إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ ٱلدُّعَآءِ
3:38.translation: Thereat Zechariah supplicated his Lord. He said, ‘My Lord! Grant me a good offspring from You! Indeed You hear all supplications.’

gems.title: Inspired Prayer
gems.insight: Witnessing Mary's miracles inspired Zechariah to pray for his own child. Seeing Allah's power in action motivates us to ask for our own needs with confidence.
gems.line: His power at work in someone else's life is reason to ask for your own need with confidence.

gems.title: Pure Offspring
gems.insight: Zechariah asks for 'good offspring' (dhurriyyatan tayyibah) - children who are pure in character and righteous in conduct, not just biological descendants.
gems.line: Zechariah asked for goodness in his children, not just children - the quality was the prayer.

gems.title: From Your Presence
gems.insight: Zechariah asks for offspring 'from You' (min ladunka) - acknowledging that children are a gift directly from Allah's presence, not merely biological outcomes.
gems.line: 'From You' - a child, and every real gift, comes from His presence, not merely from circumstance.

gems.title: Hearer of Prayer
gems.insight: Zechariah concludes by affirming Allah as 'Hearer of supplication' (Sami' ad-du'a), expressing confidence that his prayer will be heard.
gems.line: The prayer closes on certainty: He is the Hearer of supplication - no ask of Him goes unheard.

lines.text: When the truth was put on trial, God reached not for a sword but for a purified family.
One word - purified - travels from Maryam's prayer-niche to the five beneath the cloak.

3:38.morning: Zechariah saw what Allah gave Mary and asked for his own. What you see of His power is an invitation.
3:38.night: Whatever you asked Him for today reached the Hearer of supplication - Zechariah's certainty is yours to keep.

6:162.arabic: قُلْ إِنَّ صَلَاتِى وَنُسُكِى وَمَحْيَاىَ وَمَمَاتِى لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
6:162.translation: Say, ‘Indeed my prayer and my worship, my life and my death are for the sake of Allah, the Lord of all the worlds.

gems.title: Complete Devotion
gems.insight: Prayer, sacrifice, living, and dying all belong to Allah, establishing that every aspect of existence should be dedicated to the Creator.
gems.line: Nothing of you sits outside the dedication - prayer, sacrifice, the whole of life, pointed one way.

gems.title: Prayer & Sacrifice
gems.insight: Salat and nusuk (ritual acts) are explicitly for Allah alone, making worship the most visible expression of our total submission.
gems.line: Prayer and sacrifice are named first - worship is where devotion to Him alone becomes visible.

gems.title: Existence for Allah
gems.insight: Living and dying are both for Allah, making our entire temporal existence and its end purposeful acts of devotion.
gems.line: Your existence and its end are both for Him - no stretch of the span you are living is aimless.

lines.text: I love not those that set.
A heart made for God can chase the setting lights its whole life and never once feel held.
There was never a second pile: a whole life, prayer to final breath, turned one direction.

6:162.morning: The verse gives today its direction: prayer, sacrifice, and living itself - all for the Lord of the worlds.
6:162.night: The day ends inside the dedication it began with: a life that belongs, all of it, to the Lord of the worlds.

7:55.arabic: ٱدْعُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ تَضَرُّعًۭا وَخُفْيَةً ۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُعْتَدِينَ
7:55.translation: Supplicate your Lord, beseechingly and secretly. Indeed, He does not like the transgressors.

gems.title: Humble Supplication
gems.insight: Call upon Allah 'tadarru'an' (in humility) and 'khufyah' (privately), showing that effective prayer combines outward humbleness acknowledging our neediness with inward sincerity away from showing off.
gems.line: Prayer asks for two things the verse names: real humility, and privacy that keeps it pure.

gems.title: Rejecting Excess
gems.insight: Allah 'does not like transgressors' ('la yuhibb al-mu'tadin'), referring to those who exceed bounds in supplication - asking for harmful things, being impatient, or making demands rather than requests.
gems.line: Asking is welcome; demanding is not - supplication keeps its manners even at its most urgent.

gems.title: Private Connection
gems.insight: The emphasis on private supplication ('khufyah') protects the purity of our relationship with Allah from contamination by ego, social pressure, or desire for praise from others.
gems.line: What you ask Him in secret stays clean - no audience, no performing, just you and Him.

lines.text: You said yes once, before you can remember; your life is the second time you are asked.
They walked in as Pharaoh's hired magicians at sunrise; before sunset they were martyrs.
Pride, heedlessness, or a slow letting-go: every fall in al-A'raf is one promise slipping.

7:55.morning: The door for today's needs opens a particular way: humbly, and in private - that is how He asked to be called.
7:55.night: This hour is the verse's own setting - humble, private words to Him fit the night exactly.

12:86.arabic: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَشْكُوا۟ بَثِّى وَحُزْنِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَأَعْلَمُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
12:86.translation: He said, ‘I complain of my anguish and grief only to Allah. I know from Allah what you do not know.’

gems.title: Complaint to Allah
gems.insight: Yaqub says 'I only complain of my suffering and grief to Allah' - directing his pain to the Divine, not to creation.
gems.line: Grief spoken to Him is not weakness - Yaqub aimed his pain at the only One who can answer it.

gems.title: Knowledge from Allah
gems.insight: He declares 'I know from Allah what you do not know' - prophetic insight gives him certainty about outcomes hidden from others.
gems.line: Yaqub held certainty others lacked - what he knew from Allah outweighed what they knew of loss.

gems.title: Deep Suffering
gems.insight: He mentions 'bathi' (overwhelming anguish) alongside 'huzn' (grief) - distinguishing intense, debilitating sorrow from ordinary sadness.
gems.line: The verse names anguish beside grief - the Qur'an distinguishes sorrow's depths and shames neither.

gems.title: Hidden Hope
gems.insight: Despite his sons' concern, Yaqub maintains hope rooted in divine knowledge, showing grief and hope can coexist in prophetic hearts.
gems.line: Grief and hope shared one prophetic heart - sorrow did not cancel his certainty in Allah.

lines.text: No blame upon you today. May God forgive you, and He is the most merciful of the merciful.
Beautiful patience is the certainty that God keeps an account no darkness can erase.
Every pit was a road; from the well to the throne, not one hour was wasted.

12:86.morning: Yaqub set the direction for sorrow: complaint carried to Allah travels upward, not around.
12:86.night: Whatever ached today can travel Yaqub's route tonight: suffering and grief complained only to Allah.

12:101.arabic: ۞ رَبِّ قَدْ ءَاتَيْتَنِى مِنَ ٱلْمُلْكِ وَعَلَّمْتَنِى مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحَادِيثِ ۚ فَاطِرَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ أَنتَ وَلِىِّۦ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةِ ۖ تَوَفَّنِى مُسْلِمًۭا وَأَلْحِقْنِى بِٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
12:101.translation: ‘My Lord! You have granted me a share in the kingdom, and taught me the interpretation of dreams. Originator of the heavens and earth! You are my guardian in this world and the Hereafter! Let my death be in submission [to You], and unite me with the Righteous.’

gems.title: Divine Sovereignty
gems.insight: Yusuf acknowledges that his kingdom and authority are gifts from Allah, not personal achievements. True sovereignty belongs to Allah; human power is merely a temporary trust.
gems.line: Yusuf called his kingdom something given - position and power are held in trust, never owned.

gems.title: Knowledge of Dreams
gems.insight: Allah taught Yusuf the interpretation of dreams (ta'wil al-ahadith), a specialized prophetic knowledge. This gift proved crucial in his rise from prisoner to minister.
gems.line: His reading of dreams was taught, not talent - the gift that raised him came from Allah first.

gems.title: Eternal Guardian
gems.insight: Yusuf calls Allah his 'Wali' (Guardian/Protector) in this life and the hereafter. True security comes from Allah's guardianship, which extends beyond death into eternal life.
gems.line: 'You are my protector in this world and the Hereafter' - guardianship that outlasts everything.

gems.title: Die as Muslim
gems.insight: Yusuf's ultimate prayer is to die as a Muslim (in submission to Allah) and join the righteous. Despite all worldly success, his focus remains on a good ending and eternal salvation.
gems.line: After all his success, Yusuf's ask was the ending - to finish in submission, with the righteous.

lines.text: No blame upon you today. May God forgive you, and He is the most merciful of the merciful.
Beautiful patience is the certainty that God keeps an account no darkness can erase.
Every pit was a road; from the well to the throne, not one hour was wasted.

12:101.morning: Yusuf named his rank and knowledge as gifts received - what you hold today was likewise given.
12:101.night: Yusuf's prayer suits the day's end: You are my protector in this world and in the Hereafter.

14:40.arabic: رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْنِى مُقِيمَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِى ۚ رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعَآءِ
14:40.translation: My Lord! Make me a maintainer of prayer, and my descendants [as well]. Our Lord, accept my supplication.

gems.title: Prayer Establisher
gems.insight: Ibrahim asked to be made an establisher of prayer - not just one who prays, but one who upholds it as a cornerstone of life.
gems.line: An establisher of prayer holds it up as a cornerstone - prayer as structure, not just habit.

gems.title: Pious Offspring
gems.insight: Ibrahim prayed for his descendants to establish prayer - showing a parent's highest wish is their children's spiritual success.
gems.line: Ibrahim asked prayer for his descendants too - a parent's highest wish is the children's faith.

gems.title: Acceptance Plea
gems.insight: Ibrahim concluded with 'accept my supplication' - acknowledging all depends on Allah's acceptance, not just our asking.
gems.line: The dua ends with 'accept my supplication' - the asking is ours, the acceptance is His alone.

lines.text: A good word is like a good tree: its root is firm, and its branch reaches into the sky.
I am the prayer of my father Ibrahim.
What is planted with God in dead ground is never wasted; it grows while you are gone.

14:40.morning: Ibrahim did not ask merely to pray - he asked to be made an establisher of prayer. That is today's aim.
14:40.night: The prayers of your day close the way Ibrahim closed his: Our Lord, accept my supplication.

21:89.arabic: وَزَكَرِيَّآ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥ رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْنِى فَرْدًۭا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلْوَٰرِثِينَ
