39:9.translation: Is he who supplicates in the watches of the night, prostrating and standing, apprehensive of the Hereafter and expecting the mercy of his Lord...? Say, ‘Are those who know equal to those who do not know?’ Only those who possess intellect take admonition.

gems.title: Night Worshipper
gems.insight: Qanit (devoutly obedient) during night hours, alternating between prostration and standing—night prayer shows sincerity free from showing off.
gems.line: Qanit in the night hours - devotion no one sees carries a sincerity daylight cannot prove.

gems.title: Hereafter Awareness
gems.insight: Yahdharu al-akhira (fearing the Hereafter) means conscious awareness that this life is temporary and accountability is coming.
gems.line: Yahdharu al-akhira - living aware that this life is temporary keeps accountability in view.

gems.title: Balanced Hope
gems.insight: True believers balance fear (yahdharu) with hope (yarju)—afraid of punishment but hopeful for Allah's mercy, never despairing or complacent.
gems.line: Fear and hope travel paired - wary of the Hereafter, hopeful of His mercy, neither one alone.

gems.title: Unequal Status
gems.insight: Those who know (ya'lamun) are not equal to those who don't know (la ya'lamun)—knowledge of Allah and His commands elevates spiritual rank.
gems.line: The knower and the non-knower are declared unequal - knowledge of Him raises spiritual rank.

39:9.morning: Knowledge sets ranks today - the one who knows Him and the one who does not are not the same.
39:9.night: The night hours the verse honors are here - devotion now, unseen by anyone, is the sincerity it praises.

41:53.arabic: سَنُرِيهِمْ ءَايَٰتِنَا فِى ٱلْءَافَاقِ وَفِىٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ ۗ أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ أَنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ شَهِيدٌ
41:53.translation: Soon We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and in their own souls until it becomes clear to them that He is the Real. Is it not sufficient that your Lord is witness to all things?

gems.title: Universal Signs
gems.insight: Allah will show His signs 'in the horizons' (فِى ٱلْءَافَاقِ)—the external universe, cosmic phenomena, natural wonders—making divine truth evident through observable reality.
gems.line: The sky, the seasons, the working cosmos - the horizons hold His signs in plain, observable view.

gems.title: Internal Signs
gems.insight: Allah will show signs 'within themselves' (فِىٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ)—human consciousness, psychology, the soul's innate recognition of truth, our very existence and design.
gems.line: You are evidence too - consciousness, design, the soul's pull toward truth are signs within you.

gems.title: Truth Becomes Manifest
gems.insight: The purpose of these signs is 'until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth' (حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ)—an inevitable clarity that removes all doubt.
gems.line: The showing has a destination - signs keep arriving until the truth stands clear beyond doubt.

gems.title: Allah as Witness
gems.insight: The verse concludes with a rhetorical question: 'Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness?' (شَهِيدٌ)—Allah's direct witnessing supersedes all other proof.
gems.line: Past every sign stands the surest proof named here - your Lord Himself, Witness over all things.

41:53.morning: The signs promised here surround your day - in the horizons out there, and within your own self.
41:53.night: Signs filled this day, outer and inner - and over all of it, your Lord remained Witness.

45:13.arabic: وَسَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا مِّنْهُ ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍۢ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
45:13.translation: He has disposed for you[r benefit] whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth; all is from Him. There are indeed signs in that for a people who reflect.

gems.title: All Subjected
gems.insight: Everything in heavens and earth is subjected to humanity (سَخَّرَ لَكُم), demonstrating human's honored status in creation.
gems.line: The cosmos is set to serve you - an honored standing in creation you did nothing to earn.

gems.title: All From Allah
gems.insight: The phrase 'all from Him' (جَمِيعًۭا مِّنْهُ) emphasizes that every blessing, natural resource, and cosmic phenomenon originates from Allah alone.
gems.line: 'All from Him' - every blessing and resource in use today traces to a single origin.

gems.title: Signs for Thinkers
gems.insight: These are signs 'for people who give thought' (يَتَفَكَّرُونَ), meaning deep reflection reveals Allah's wisdom in cosmic design.
gems.line: The signs unlock at the level of thought - reflection turns scenery into evidence.

45:13.morning: Everything serving you today - sun, sea, the ground underfoot - was subjected for you, all from Him.
45:13.night: A day spent inside His subjected world ends - those who gave it thought saw signs all through it.

47:24.arabic: أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ أَمْ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبٍ أَقْفَالُهَآ
47:24.translation: Do they not contemplate the Quran, or are there locks on the hearts?

gems.title: Quranic Reflection
gems.insight: 'Do they not reflect upon the Quran?' (تَدَبَّرُونَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ)—tadabbur means deep, contemplative reflection, not surface reading. The Quran demands intellectual and spiritual engagement.
gems.line: Tadabbur is not skimming - the Book expects mind and heart engaged, not recitation alone.

gems.title: Locked Hearts
gems.insight: 'Or are there locks upon their hearts?' (أَقْفَالُهَآ)—some hearts are locked from within, self-imposed barriers preventing Quranic truth from entering.
gems.line: The locks the verse mentions are fitted from within - the barriers to truth are self-imposed.

gems.title: Challenging Question
gems.insight: This rhetorical question indicts those who hear the Quran but remain unchanged—forcing them to admit either they don't reflect, or their hearts are locked.
gems.line: For the unmoved hearer the verse leaves two explanations - no reflection, or a locked heart.

gems.title: Unlocking Wisdom
gems.insight: The cure for locked hearts is tadabbur (reflection)—the Quran itself provides the key to unlock its treasures if we approach it with sincere contemplation.
gems.line: The key is named beside the lock - sincere contemplation is how the Qur'an opens its treasures.

47:24.morning: The Qur'an asks for more than your eyes today - tadabbur, the slow reflection that lets it in.
47:24.night: A locked heart is not a sentence - honest reflection tonight is the key the verse itself points to.

49:6.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِن جَآءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌۢ بِنَبَإٍۢ فَتَبَيَّنُوٓا۟ أَن تُصِيبُوا۟ قَوْمًۢا بِجَهَٰلَةٍۢ فَتُصْبِحُوا۟ عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلْتُمْ نَٰدِمِينَ
49:6.translation: O you who have faith! If a vicious character brings you some news, verify it, lest you should visit [harm] on some people out of ignorance, and then become regretful for what you have done.

gems.title: Verify First
gems.insight: Believers are commanded to verify information brought by a fasiq (disobedient/unreliable person) before acting on it, establishing the principle of evidence-based judgment.
gems.line: The unreliable report is not ignored but checked - judgment waits for evidence before it moves.

gems.title: Preventing Harm
gems.insight: The verse warns against harming innocent people out of ignorance, emphasizing that good intentions don't excuse actions based on unverified claims.
gems.line: Good intentions do not excuse acting on unverified claims - the innocent pay the cost of haste.

gems.title: Avoiding Regret
gems.insight: The warning about becoming regretful highlights that hasty actions based on false information lead to lasting remorse that could have been avoided.
gems.line: Regret is the verse's forecast for haste - remorse that verification would have prevented.

49:6.morning: Reports will reach you today - this verse sets a pause before belief, so ignorance harms no one.
49:6.night: Every claim you checked before acting today closed the road to the verse's ending - lasting regret.

59:21.arabic: لَوْ أَنزَلْنَا هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ عَلَىٰ جَبَلٍۢ لَّرَأَيْتَهُۥ خَٰشِعًۭا مُّتَصَدِّعًۭا مِّنْ خَشْيَةِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ وَتِلْكَ ٱلْأَمْثَٰلُ نَضْرِبُهَا لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
59:21.translation: Had We sent down this Quran upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled [and] go to pieces with the fear of Allah. We draw such comparisons for mankind, so that they may reflect.

gems.title: Quran's Power
gems.insight: If the Quran were sent upon a mountain, the mountain would humble itself and split apart from fear of Allah - yet human hearts remain harder than stone.
gems.line: A mountain would humble itself and crack under this Word - hearts are asked to be softer than stone.

gems.title: Khushu - Humility
gems.insight: 'Khashi'an' (humbled) describes the mountain's posture - true humility before Allah's word involves total submission, not just external rituals.
gems.line: Khashi'an - the mountain's humbling is total submission, the posture the Word deserves.

gems.title: Splitting Apart
gems.insight: 'Mutasaddi'an' (splitting apart) shows the Quran's power to shatter even the hardest creation - it should break our egos, assumptions, and spiritual complacency.
gems.line: Mutasaddi'an - the Word can break apart what is hardest, ego and complacency included.

gems.title: Divine Parables
gems.insight: Allah presents parables 'so they might reflect' - these examples aren't just illustrations but catalysts for deep contemplation about our spiritual state.
gems.line: The parables are set out for reflection - each one an invitation to examine your own state.

59:21.morning: Had this Qur'an descended on a mountain, it would split from the fear of Allah - today it meets your heart.
59:21.night: The verse leaves its measure with you tonight - a Book that would have humbled and split a mountain.

2:188.arabic: وَلَا تَأْكُلُوٓا۟ أَمْوَٰلَكُم بَيْنَكُم بِٱلْبَٰطِلِ وَتُدْلُوا۟ بِهَآ إِلَى ٱلْحُكَّامِ لِتَأْكُلُوا۟ فَرِيقًۭا مِّنْ أَمْوَٰلِ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلْإِثْمِ وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
2:188.translation: Do not eat up your wealth among yourselves wrongfully, nor proffer it to the judges in order to eat up a part of the people’s wealth sinfully, while you know [that it is immoral to do so].

gems.title: Wealth Ethics
gems.insight: Consuming others' wealth through falsehood (batil) is strictly forbidden—this includes fraud, deception, theft, and any transaction lacking genuine consent or fairness.
gems.line: Fraud, deception, a deal without true consent - the verse calls all of it by one name: batil.

gems.title: Bribery Forbidden
gems.insight: Bribing judges to consume others' wealth unlawfully is explicitly condemned. The verse addresses both those who bribe and corrupt officials who accept.
gems.line: A bribe stains both hands - the one that offers it and the one that opens for it.

gems.title: Conscious Wrongdoing
gems.insight: The phrase 'while you know' emphasizes that knowingly committing financial crimes is especially grave—ignorance may excuse, but deliberate sin compounds guilt.
gems.line: 'While you know' is the sharpest phrase: wrongdoing done knowingly carries double weight.

lines.text: I have submitted to the Lord of all the worlds.
The cow God asked for was free; the cow their questions built cost its weight in gold.
Obedience was always the shortest road; only our questions ever made it long.

2:188.morning: What you earn today is worth keeping clean - nothing taken falsely is worth what it costs.
2:188.night: What you refused to take today never becomes a weight you carry tonight.

4:1.arabic: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُوا۟ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍۢ وَٰحِدَةٍۢ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًۭا كَثِيرًۭا وَنِسَآءًۭ ۚ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِى تَسَآءَلُونَ بِهِۦ وَٱلْأَرْحَامَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًۭا
4:1.translation: O mankind! Be wary of your Lord who created you from a single soul, and created its mate from it, and from the two of them scattered numerous men and women. Be wary of Allah, in whose Name you adjure one another and [of severing ties with] blood relations. Indeed Allah is watchful over you.

gems.title: Common Origin
gems.insight: All humanity originates from a single soul (nafs wahida), emphasizing our shared human dignity and equality before Allah.
gems.line: One soul began every lineage - the stranger passing you today is distant family by origin.

gems.title: Sacred Wombs
gems.insight: The verse commands to 'fear the wombs' (al-arham), recognizing motherhood as sacred and demanding respect for family bonds and women's dignity.
gems.line: 'Fear Allah and the wombs' - family bonds and the mothers who formed you carry sacred weight.

gems.title: Divine Observer
gems.insight: Allah is described as Raqib (Ever-Watchful Observer), reminding us that every action concerning family rights is witnessed and recorded.
gems.line: He is Raqib, the Ever-Watchful - how family rights are handled today does not go unseen.

gems.title: Fear of Allah
gems.insight: The surah opens with a call to taqwa (God-consciousness), establishing that all social laws that follow are rooted in spiritual awareness.
gems.line: The surah roots its social law in taqwa first - how you treat people begins with awareness of Him.

lines.text: Taste this, Ali - taste the fire. This is for the one who fails the widow and the orphan.
A right on a page protects no one; every right is a trust placed in someone's hands.
Obedience closes the distance that love alone cannot close.

4:1.morning: Every person you meet today traces back with you to one soul - a kinship older than any difference.
4:1.night: Family and stranger alike today shared your origin - and the Observer saw how each one was met.

4:40.arabic: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَظْلِمُ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍۢ ۖ وَإِن تَكُ حَسَنَةًۭ يُضَٰعِفْهَا وَيُؤْتِ مِن لَّدُنْهُ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًۭا
4:40.translation: Indeed Allah does not wrong [anyone] [even to the extent of] an atom’s weight, and if it be a good deed He doubles it[s reward], and gives from Himself a great reward.

gems.title: Perfect Justice
gems.insight: Allah does not commit injustice (zulm) even the weight of an atom (mithqal dharrah). Every deed, however small, is weighed with absolute precision.
gems.line: Not an atom's weight of injustice touches His accounting - your smallest deed is weighed precisely.

gems.title: Divine Multiplication
gems.insight: When there is a good deed (hasanah), Allah multiplies it (yuda'ifha). The Quran elsewhere specifies this can be 10x to 700x or more, while sins are counted as-is.
gems.line: One good deed never stays one with Him - it is multiplied, while sins are counted only as they are.

gems.title: Divine Gift
gems.insight: Beyond multiplication, Allah gives from Himself (min ladunhu) a great reward (ajran 'azima). This is a bonus beyond the earned reward - pure divine generosity.
gems.line: After the multiplying comes more - a great reward from Himself, generosity beyond what you earned.

lines.text: Taste this, Ali - taste the fire. This is for the one who fails the widow and the orphan.
A right on a page protects no one; every right is a trust placed in someone's hands.
Obedience closes the distance that love alone cannot close.

4:40.morning: Nothing good you do today can be lost - He does not do injustice even by an atom's weight.
4:40.night: If any good passed through your hands today, it is already multiplied - and His gift comes on top.

4:58.arabic: ۞ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تُؤَدُّوا۟ ٱلْأَمَٰنَٰتِ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهَا وَإِذَا حَكَمْتُم بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ أَن تَحْكُمُوا۟ بِٱلْعَدْلِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ نِعِمَّا يَعِظُكُم بِهِۦٓ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ سَمِيعًۢا بَصِيرًۭا
4:58.translation: Indeed Allah commands you to deliver the trusts to their [rightful] owners, and to judge with fairness when you judge between people. Excellent indeed is what Allah advises you. Indeed Allah is all-hearing, all-seeing.

gems.title: Return Trusts
gems.insight: Amanat (trust) includes everything entrusted to us—possessions, secrets, responsibilities, authority. Returning trusts to rightful owners is a divine command, not a social suggestion.
gems.line: Returning what was entrusted to you is a command from Him, not a courtesy you may skip.

gems.title: Just Judgment
gems.insight: Judging with justice when holding authority is paired with returning trusts—both are aspects of fulfilling our responsibilities toward others with fairness and honesty.
gems.line: Wherever your word decides something for others today, fairness is part of the trust.

gems.title: Divine Counsel
gems.insight: Allah praises His own instruction as 'excellent'—emphasizing that divine commands are not arbitrary burdens but beneficial wisdom that elevates human society.
gems.line: His instruction is called excellent by Him - what He asks of you is wisdom, not burden.

gems.title: Complete Awareness
gems.insight: Allah is 'Hearing and Seeing'—He witnesses both the words we speak when judging and the actions we take when handling trusts. Nothing escapes His observation.
gems.line: He hears the words you judge with and sees how you handle what was entrusted - all of it.

lines.text: Taste this, Ali - taste the fire. This is for the one who fails the widow and the orphan.
A right on a page protects no one; every right is a trust placed in someone's hands.
Obedience closes the distance that love alone cannot close.

4:58.morning: Everything placed in your hands today - things, secrets, duties - is a trust with a rightful owner.
4:58.night: The trusts of this day - what you returned, what you judged - passed before One who hears and sees.

4:135.arabic: ۞ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُونُوا۟ قَوَّٰمِينَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ شُهَدَآءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَوِ ٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ وَٱلْأَقْرَبِينَ ۚ إِن يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًۭا فَٱللَّهُ أَوْلَىٰ بِهِمَا ۖ فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا۟ ٱلْهَوَىٰٓ أَن تَعْدِلُوا۟ ۚ وَإِن تَلْوُۥٓا۟ أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا۟ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًۭا
4:135.translation: O you who have faith! Be maintainers of justice and witnesses for the sake of Allah, even if it should be against yourselves or [your] parents and near relatives, and whether it be [someone] rich or poor, for Allah has a greater right over them. So do not follow [your] desires, lest you should be unfair, and if you distort [the testimony] or disregard [it], Allah is indeed well aware of what you do.

gems.title: Justice Above All
gems.insight: Believers must stand firmly for justice as witnesses for Allah, even if testimony is against themselves, parents, or close relatives.
gems.line: Standing for justice is witness borne for Allah - even when the testimony points at your own self.

gems.title: No Class Bias
gems.insight: Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both - don't let wealth or poverty bias your testimony or judgments.
gems.line: Rich or poor, He is closer to both than you are - neither wealth nor need may tilt your fairness.

gems.title: Resist Desire
gems.insight: Don't follow hawa (personal inclination/desire) lest you fail to be just - if you distort or refuse testimony, Allah is fully aware of what you do.
gems.line: The threat to your fairness is inward - hawa, the pull of preference, is what bends testimony.

gems.title: Divine Accountability
gems.insight: Allah is Khabir (Acquainted/Aware) of what you do, knowing when justice is upheld or corrupted, when truth is spoken or twisted.
gems.line: Twisting the truth or withholding it are both seen - He is fully acquainted with what you do.

lines.text: Taste this, Ali - taste the fire. This is for the one who fails the widow and the orphan.
A right on a page protects no one; every right is a trust placed in someone's hands.
Obedience closes the distance that love alone cannot close.

4:135.morning: Justice today may cost you something close - the verse asks for it even then, even against yourself.
4:135.night: If being fair cost you something today, it was not unnoticed - He is acquainted with what you do.

4:148.arabic: ۞ لَّا يُحِبُّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْجَهْرَ بِٱلسُّوٓءِ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ إِلَّا مَن ظُلِمَ ۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ سَمِيعًا عَلِيمًا
4:148.translation: Allah does not like the disclosure of [anyone’s] evil [conduct] in speech except by someone who has been wronged, and Allah is all-hearing, all-knowing.

gems.title: Speaking Ill
gems.insight: Allah declares He does not like public mention of evil (al-jahr bi'l-su'), meaning spreading negativity, backbiting, or publicizing sins. Such speech pollutes the social environment.
gems.line: Broadcasting faults pollutes more than it fixes - He does not love evil made loud.

gems.title: Victim's Voice
gems.insight: An exception is made for one who has been wronged (man dhulim), who is permitted to speak publicly about the injustice. This protects the right to seek justice and expose oppression.
gems.line: If you have been wronged, your voice is protected - naming injustice aloud is your right.

gems.title: Divine Witness
gems.insight: Allah describes Himself as Sami' (All-Hearing) and 'Alim (All-Knowing), meaning He hears every word spoken, whether publicly or privately, and knows the context and intention behind it.
gems.line: Public or whispered, every word lands in His hearing - and He knows the intent behind it.

lines.text: Taste this, Ali - taste the fire. This is for the one who fails the widow and the orphan.
A right on a page protects no one; every right is a trust placed in someone's hands.
Obedience closes the distance that love alone cannot close.

4:148.morning: Your words today can keep the air clean - public airing of evil is not something He loves.
4:148.night: Every word of this day was heard with its context - He is Hearing, and He is Knowing.

5:8.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُونُوا۟ قَوَّٰمِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَآءَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ ۖ وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوْمٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا۟ ۚ ٱعْدِلُوا۟ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ ۖ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرٌۢ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
5:8.translation: O you who have faith! Be maintainers, as witnesses for the sake of Allah, of justice, and ill feeling for a people should never lead you to be unfair. Be fair; that is nearer to Godwariness, and be wary of Allah. Allah is indeed well aware of what you do.

gems.title: Standing for Allah
gems.insight: Believers are commanded to be 'persistently standing firm for Allah' (qawwamin lillah). This means making Allah's pleasure the primary motivation in all affairs, establishing justice not for personal gain or social approval but purely as an act of devotion to the Creator.
gems.line: Standing firm for justice is done for Allah - not for applause, not for advantage, for Him.

gems.title: Witnesses in Justice
gems.insight: Muslims must be 'witnesses in justice' (shuhada' bil-qist), meaning they must uphold truth and fairness in all testimonies and judgments. This extends beyond courtroom testimony to every situation where one's word or assessment affects others' rights.
gems.line: Wherever your word affects someone's rights today, you are standing as a witness in justice.

gems.title: Overcoming Hatred
gems.insight: The verse explicitly warns: do not let hatred of a people lead you to be unjust. Personal animosity, historical grievances, or collective bias must never compromise one's commitment to fair treatment. Justice must be given even to enemies.
gems.line: Even the people you like least keep their claim on your fairness - dislike is no license.

gems.title: Justice and Taqwa
gems.insight: The command 'Be just - it is nearer to righteousness (taqwa)' establishes a direct connection between justice and God-consciousness. Acting justly is not merely a social virtue but a spiritual act that brings one closer to Allah and reflects true piety.
gems.line: Acting justly is itself an act of nearness - the verse ties fairness directly to taqwa.

lines.text: He whose mawla I am - whose guardian and master I am - this Ali is his mawla.
This day I have perfected for you your religion, and completed My favor upon you...
You renew the oldest pledge every time you stand to pray: we hear, and we obey.

5:8.morning: Someone may test your fairness today - the verse holds the line: no hatred may bend your justice.
5:8.night: If you stayed fair today toward someone you find hard to love, that was nearness to taqwa itself.

7:181.arabic: وَمِمَّنْ خَلَقْنَآ أُمَّةٌۭ يَهْدُونَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَبِهِۦ يَعْدِلُونَ
7:181.translation: Among those We have created are a nation who guide by the truth and do justice thereby.

gems.title: Guided Community
gems.insight: Allah affirms that among His creation exists a community (ummah) that guides by truth and establishes justice, representing the continuation of divine guidance through righteous believers.
gems.line: Guidance did not end with the prophets - a community that guides by truth is always in the world.

gems.title: Guidance by Truth
gems.insight: The phrase 'yahduna bil-haqq' (guide by truth) emphasizes that true guidance must be rooted in objective truth, not personal opinion or cultural convention.
gems.line: What guides must be true, not merely popular - opinion and custom cannot stand in for haqq.

gems.title: Justice by Truth
gems.insight: The phrase 'wa bihi ya'dilun' (and thereby establish justice) shows that true justice naturally flows from adherence to divine truth and guidance.
gems.line: Justice is not a separate project - where truth is genuinely followed, fairness follows from it.

gems.title: Created Community
gems.insight: The phrase 'mimman khalaqna' (among those We created) emphasizes that this guided community is part of Allah's deliberate creation and plan, not a random occurrence.
gems.line: That guiding community is no accident of history - He created it, deliberately, as part of His plan.

lines.text: You said yes once, before you can remember; your life is the second time you are asked.
They walked in as Pharaoh's hired magicians at sunrise; before sunset they were martyrs.
Pride, heedlessness, or a slow letting-go: every fall in al-A'raf is one promise slipping.

7:181.morning: Somewhere in the world today a community guides by truth and judges by it - and you can stand with them.
7:181.night: The verse outlasts the day: among what He created there is a people guiding by truth, judging by it.

10:44.arabic: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَظْلِمُ ٱلنَّاسَ شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلنَّاسَ أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ
10:44.translation: Indeed Allah does not wrong people in the least; rather, it is people who wrong themselves.

gems.title: Perfect Justice
gems.insight: The emphatic declaration "Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people at all" establishes divine justice as absolute. No one will be punished unjustly or denied reward unfairly. Allah's judgment is perfectly just.
gems.line: 'Allah does not wrong the people at all' - no punishment unearned, no reward unfairly withheld.

gems.title: Self-Inflicted Harm
gems.insight: The verse concludes "but it is the people who are wronging themselves." All spiritual harm is self-inflicted through bad choices. Allah provides guidance; humans harm themselves by rejecting it.
gems.line: The only harm that reaches a soul is self-chosen - His guidance stands; turning away is the injury.

gems.title: Fair Judgment
gems.insight: This verse establishes the framework for divine accountability: (1) Allah provides clear guidance, (2) humans freely choose to accept or reject, (3) consequences flow from choices, (4) Allah judges with perfect justice.
gems.line: Guidance given, choice free, consequences owned, judgment just - the whole account is fair.

lines.text: My servant keeps drawing near to Me with voluntary acts until I love him...
Pharaoh did not run out of mercy; he ran out of moments when a yes could mean anything.
Only one city ever turned in time; this surah carries its prophet's name as the proof.

10:44.morning: One certainty to carry today: whatever goes wrong, no wrong will ever come from Him.
10:44.night: Whatever went wrong today, one thing is settled: none of it was injustice from Him. He wrongs no one.

16:90.arabic: ۞ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَٱلْإِحْسَٰنِ وَإِيتَآئِ ذِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَيَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنكَرِ وَٱلْبَغْىِ ۚ يَعِظُكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ
16:90.translation: Indeed Allah enjoins justice and kindness, and generosity towards relatives, and He forbids indecency, wrongdoing, and aggression. He advises you, so that you may take admonition.

gems.title: Dual Moral Standards
gems.insight: Allah commands both justice (adl) - giving everyone their due rights - and excellence (ihsan) - going beyond what is required with generosity and beauty.
gems.line: Justice gives each person their due - excellence gives more than was owed. Today has room for both.

gems.title: Kinship Priority
gems.insight: Giving to relatives (dhi al-qurba) is specifically commanded, emphasizing family bonds and responsibilities. Charity begins with those closest to us.
gems.line: Giving starts with those closest - your relatives hold a named place in today's generosity.

gems.title: Three Prohibitions
gems.insight: Allah forbids three categories of evil: fahsha (sexual immorality), munkar (socially recognized wrongs), and baghy (transgression/oppression). This covers private sins, public evils, and social injustice.
gems.line: Private sin, public wrong, and oppression - the verse closes all three doors, hidden and seen.

gems.title: Ongoing Reminder
gems.insight: Allah admonishes (ya'izu) you continuously - this is not one-time instruction but perpetual guidance. The Quran keeps reminding us so we may remember and be mindful.
gems.line: The reminder repeats because forgetting repeats - His guidance arrives as often as you need it.

lines.text: They recognize the blessing of Allah - then they deny it.
Asked what a good life means in the Qur'an, he said: it is contentment.
The surah is named not for the pouring, but for the one who received it rightly.

16:90.morning: One verse sets today's standard: justice as the floor, excellence above it, and your own kin first in line.
16:90.night: Justice, excellence, care for kin - wherever today touched them, it stood inside this verse's command.

17:35.arabic: وَأَوْفُوا۟ ٱلْكَيْلَ إِذَا كِلْتُمْ وَزِنُوا۟ بِٱلْقِسْطَاسِ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمِ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ خَيْرٌۭ وَأَحْسَنُ تَأْوِيلًۭا
17:35.translation: When you measure, observe fully the measure, [and] weigh with an even balance. That is better and more favourable with respect to the outcome [in the Hereafter].

gems.title: Commercial Honesty
gems.insight: Commanding full measure and accurate weight in trade establishes commercial ethics as religious obligation. The 'even balance' (qistas mustaqim) demands precision and fairness in all transactions.
gems.line: Full measure and true weight are commanded - honest dealing is religion, not just good business.

gems.title: Best Outcome
gems.insight: Honesty in trade is described as 'the best way and best in result' (ahsanu ta'wila) - promising that integrity brings superior outcomes both worldly and spiritually.
gems.line: Honesty is promised the best outcome - integrity outperforms the shortcut in both worlds.

gems.title: Economic Justice
gems.insight: By mandating fair measurement, Islam creates economic justice at the transaction level. When individuals practice honesty in small dealings, entire markets remain just.
gems.line: Markets stay just one honest deal at a time - your fair transaction holds up a corner of the whole.

17:35.morning: Fair measure is worship in work clothes - every honest transaction today keeps a command of Allah.
17:35.night: Every fair measure you gave today lands where the verse said - the best way, and the best result.

21:47.arabic: وَنَضَعُ ٱلْمَوَٰزِينَ ٱلْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌۭ شَيْـًۭٔا ۖ وَإِن كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍۢ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنَا بِهَا ۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَٰسِبِينَ
21:47.translation: We shall set up just scales on the Day of Resurrection, and no soul will be wronged in the least. Even if it be the weight of a mustard seed We shall produce it and We suffice as reckoners.

gems.title: Perfect Justice
gems.insight: The scales of justice on the Day of Resurrection are perfectly calibrated. No soul faces even the slightest injustice in divine judgment.
gems.line: The scales are qist, perfectly just - judgment holds not the slightest unfairness for any soul.

gems.title: Mustard Seed Precision
gems.insight: Even an action as small as a mustard seed will be brought forth and weighed. Divine accounting misses nothing, no matter how tiny.
gems.line: A deed the weight of a mustard seed is still brought forth - smallness never disqualifies good.

gems.title: Ultimate Accountant
gems.insight: Allah declares Himself sufficient as the Accountant, needing no assistants or intermediaries. His knowledge is complete and His judgment final.
gems.line: He is sufficient as Accountant - no assistant needed, no record incomplete, no verdict unfair.

gems.title: Zero Injustice
gems.insight: The emphatic 'no soul will be treated unjustly at all' removes any fear that good deeds go unrewarded or innocence gets punished.
gems.line: 'No soul will be treated unjustly at all' - no good unrewarded, no innocence punished.

21:47.morning: The scales set for the Day of Resurrection are exact - nothing done today will be lost or miscounted.
21:47.night: Nothing from today slipped the record - a mustard seed's weight of good is enough to be brought forth.

26:183.arabic: وَلَا تَبْخَسُوا۟ ٱلنَّاسَ أَشْيَآءَهُمْ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ
26:183.translation: and do not cheat the people of their goods. Do not act wickedly on the earth, causing corruption.

gems.title: Human Rights
gems.insight: The phrase 'do not deprive people of their things' establishes that every person has rights (ashya'ahum - their things) that must be respected.
gems.line: Ashya'ahum - their things - what belongs to people is theirs by right, and rights are guarded.

gems.title: Societal Corruption
gems.insight: The command prohibits 'spreading corruption on earth' (mufsideen), showing that economic injustice doesn't just harm individuals but corrupts entire societies.
gems.line: Shortchanging is never contained - one person cheated feeds corruption across the earth.

gems.title: Individual & Collective
gems.insight: The verse addresses two levels of harm: individual (depriving people) and systemic (corrupting the earth), showing sin has both personal and societal dimensions.
gems.line: The verse counts the harm twice - once against the person, once against the society around them.

26:183.morning: Today's dealings carry a revealed instruction: no one leaves your hands with less than their due.
26:183.night: If your dealings today left no one short, both of the verse's commands were kept in your hands.

33:35.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ وَٱلْمُسْلِمَٰتِ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ وَٱلْقَٰنِتِينَ وَٱلْقَٰنِتَٰتِ وَٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ وَٱلصَّٰدِقَٰتِ وَٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ وَٱلصَّٰبِرَٰتِ وَٱلْخَٰشِعِينَ وَٱلْخَٰشِعَٰتِ وَٱلْمُتَصَدِّقِينَ وَٱلْمُتَصَدِّقَٰتِ وَٱلصَّٰٓئِمِينَ وَٱلصَّٰٓئِمَٰتِ وَٱلْحَٰفِظِينَ فُرُوجَهُمْ وَٱلْحَٰفِظَٰتِ وَٱلذَّٰكِرِينَ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرًۭا وَٱلذَّٰكِرَٰتِ أَعَدَّ ٱللَّهُ لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةًۭ وَأَجْرًا عَظِيمًۭا
33:35.translation: Indeed the muslim men and the muslim women, the faithful men and the faithful women, the obedient men and the obedient women, the truthful men and the truthful women, the patient men and the patient women, the humble men and the humble women, the charitable men and the charitable women, the men who fast and the women who fast, the men who guard their private parts and the women who guard, the men who remember Allah greatly and the women who remember [Allah greatly] - Allah holds in store for them forgiveness and a great reward.

gems.title: Spiritual Equality
gems.insight: This comprehensive verse pairs men and women in ten spiritual categories, establishing that both genders share equal access to divine reward and spiritual achievement.
gems.line: The verse pairs men and women through every virtue - His reward reaches both alike.

gems.title: Ten Virtues
gems.insight: The verse lists ten paired virtues: submission, faith, obedience, truthfulness, patience, humility, charity, fasting, chastity, and constant remembrance of Allah.
gems.line: The ten named virtues sketch a whole life - from inward faith to fasting to guarded modesty.

gems.title: Constant Dhikr
gems.insight: The climax of the list is 'remembering Allah often' (dhikr kathir), suggesting that constant remembrance is the crown of all spiritual virtues.
gems.line: The list rises to its crown: remembering Allah often - the virtue that carries all the others.

gems.title: Great Reward
gems.insight: Allah promises 'maghfira' (forgiveness) and 'ajr azim' (great reward) for those who cultivate these qualities, emphasizing both mercy and generous compensation.
gems.line: For their keepers He has prepared two things by name: forgiveness, and a great reward.

33:35.morning: Ten virtues, each named twice - for men and for women alike - and all of them are open today.
33:35.night: Whichever of the ten virtues today touched, the same preparation stands: forgiveness and great reward.

41:46.arabic: مَّنْ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا فَلِنَفْسِهِۦ ۖ وَمَنْ أَسَآءَ فَعَلَيْهَا ۗ وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِظَلَّٰمٍۢ لِّلْعَبِيدِ
41:46.translation: Whoever acts righteously, it is for [the benefit of] his own soul, and whoever does evil, it is to its detriment, and your Lord is not tyrannical to His servants.

gems.title: Personal Accountability
gems.insight: Every righteous deed benefits the doer's own soul, while every evil act harms only the perpetrator. This verse establishes the principle of individual moral responsibility.
gems.line: What you do is done first to yourself - righteousness is for your soul, evil is against it.

gems.title: Divine Justice
gems.insight: Allah emphatically declares He is not unjust to His servants, using the intensive form 'not ever unjust'. This affirms that all divine judgments are perfectly just.
gems.line: The wording is emphatic - your Lord is not ever unjust to His servants; every verdict is fair.

gems.title: Self-Contained Impact
gems.insight: Good deeds and bad deeds create a self-contained cycle where consequences return to their originator. No one else bears the weight of another's sins or gains credit for another's virtues.
gems.line: No one else carries your sins, and no one else collects your good - the return is all your own.

gems.title: Servants' Dignity
gems.insight: Allah refers to humans as 'servants' (العبيد), acknowledging our honored relationship with Him. Combined with His justice, this shows divine care for human dignity.
gems.line: Even in judgment He calls you His servant - an honored relation, guarded by His perfect justice.

41:46.morning: Every deed you choose today lands on your own ledger - good feeds your soul, evil weighs against it.
41:46.night: Whatever you did today has already found its address - your own soul. And your Lord wrongs no one.

45:22.arabic: وَخَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلِتُجْزَىٰ كُلُّ نَفْسٍۭ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ
45:22.translation: Allah created the heavens and the earth with consummate wisdom, so that every soul may be requited for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.

gems.title: Purposeful Creation
gems.insight: The heavens and earth weren't created randomly or frivolously but with truth (bil-haqq) - meaning, purpose, and moral structure are built into existence.
gems.line: Nothing about existence is frivolous - creation came with haqq, meaning built into its structure.

gems.title: Personal Accountability
gems.insight: Every soul (nafs) will be individually recompensed for what it earned - accountability is personal, not collective or transferable.
gems.line: Recompense is counted per soul - what you earned is yours to answer for, and only yours.

gems.title: Perfect Justice
gems.insight: Divine judgment carries zero injustice (la yuthlamun) - no good deed overlooked, no sin exaggerated, perfect fairness guaranteed.
gems.line: 'They will not be wronged' - no good deed slips the record, no fault written larger than it was.

45:22.morning: The world you step into today was built with truth - purpose and moral order are in its frame.
45:22.night: Today's earnings rest with a Judge who wrongs no one - the fairness of the count is guaranteed.

49:13.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍۢ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلْنَٰكُمْ شُعُوبًۭا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓا۟ ۚ إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتْقَىٰكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌۭ
49:13.translation: O mankind! Indeed, We created you from a male and a female, and made you nations and tribes that you may identify yourselves with one another. Indeed the noblest of you in the sight of Allah is the most Godwary among you. Indeed Allah is all-knowing, all-aware.

gems.title: Common Origin
gems.insight: All humanity is created from a single male and female, establishing fundamental equality regardless of race, color, or ethnicity - we share common ancestors.
gems.line: All of humanity descends from one male and one female - lineage marks origin, never worth.

gems.title: Know Each Other
gems.insight: Peoples and tribes exist for mutual recognition and acquaintance, not competition or superiority - diversity is designed for connection, understanding, and learning.
gems.line: Peoples and tribes exist for knowing one another - difference is an invitation, not a wall.

gems.title: Taqwa Criterion
gems.insight: The most noble person in Allah's sight is the one with greatest taqwa, establishing God-consciousness as the only valid criterion for human excellence.
gems.line: Nobility with Allah is measured by taqwa alone - every other ranking falls away before Him.

gems.title: Allah Knows All
gems.insight: The verse concludes that Allah is Aleem (All-Knowing) and Khabeer (All-Aware), reminding us that only Allah truly knows each person's spiritual rank.
gems.line: He is Knowing, Acquainted - each soul's true rank is His knowledge, not anyone's to assign.

49:13.morning: Everyone you meet today shares your origin - and the only rank Allah counts is taqwa.
49:13.night: Whatever rankings today ran on, one stands tonight: the most noble with Allah is the most God-conscious.

55:9.arabic: وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلْوَزْنَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ وَلَا تُخْسِرُوا۟ ٱلْمِيزَانَ
55:9.translation: Maintain the weights with justice, and do not shorten the balance!’

gems.title: Establish Weight
gems.insight: 'Aqimu al-wazn' (establish weight) commands active implementation of justice with precision and care. Justice requires deliberate effort and attention.
gems.line: Justice is established, not assumed - fairness in today's dealings takes deliberate care.

gems.title: With Justice
gems.insight: 'Bil-qist' (with justice) emphasizes that fairness must be the foundation. Even correct procedures mean nothing without genuine commitment to equity.
gems.line: Correct form without honest fairness fails the verse - qist is equity meant, not performed.

gems.title: Prevent Cheating
gems.insight: 'Wa la tukhsiru al-mizan' (do not make deficient the balance) prohibits any form of cheating or shortchanging, whether in commerce or human relations.
gems.line: Shortchanging in any form tips the balance - in trade and in dealings between people alike.

lines.text: None of Your favors, my Lord, do I deny.
Guidance was prepared before you existed, the way a cradle is made ready before a birth.
Everything passes; what remains is not a cold survivor but generosity that stays.

55:9.morning: 'Establish weight in justice' covers today whole - every measure, price, and judgment you touch.
55:9.night: Every scale you touched today - goods, judgments, words - sat under one command: do not tip it.

60:8.arabic: لَّا يَنْهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمْ يُقَٰتِلُوكُمْ فِى ٱلدِّينِ وَلَمْ يُخْرِجُوكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِكُمْ أَن تَبَرُّوهُمْ وَتُقْسِطُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُقْسِطِينَ
60:8.translation: Allah does not forbid you from dealing with kindness and justice with those [polytheists] who did not make war against you on account of religion and did not expel you from your homes. Indeed Allah loves the just.

gems.title: Justice with Non-Combatants
gems.insight: Allah permits righteous and just treatment toward those who neither fight believers for their faith nor expel them from their homes.
gems.line: Kindness and fairness to the peaceable are not concessions - Allah Himself permits them.

gems.title: Righteousness (Birr)
gems.insight: The term 'birr' (righteousness) is used for treatment of peaceful non-Muslims - the same word used for honoring parents, indicating high ethical standards.
gems.line: Birr - the word used for honoring parents - is the standard set for treating the peaceable.

gems.title: Divine Love for Justice
gems.insight: Allah loves those who act justly - fairness and equity are beloved qualities that earn divine pleasure regardless of who receives the justice.
gems.line: 'Allah loves those who act justly' - fairness earns His love, whoever is on the receiving end.

60:8.morning: Toward those who mean you no harm, the verse opens the door wide - be righteous with them, be just.
60:8.night: Where you dealt fairly today, the verse's close already applies - Allah loves those who act justly.

95:8.translation: Is not Allah the fairest of all judges?

gems.title: Supreme Judge
gems.insight: 'Ahkam al-Hakimeen' (most just of judges) affirms Allah as the ultimate arbiter whose judgments are perfectly fair and absolutely wise.
gems.line: Every verdict from Him comes from ahkam al-hakimin - fairness has no higher court than His.

gems.title: Rhetorical Affirmation
gems.insight: The question 'Alaysa Allahu...' (Is not Allah...) expects an emphatic 'Yes!' - it's an undeniable truth no rational person can reject.
gems.line: The question is asked so the answer can only be yes - a truth no honest reasoning can refuse.

gems.title: Divine Wisdom
gems.insight: Allah's judgment (hukm) combines perfect knowledge, absolute justice, and infinite wisdom - surpassing any human court or understanding.
gems.line: His judgment holds what no human court does - complete knowledge, pure justice, and wisdom entire.

gems.title: Believer's Response
gems.insight: Muslims traditionally respond 'Bala, wa ana ala dhalika min ash-shahideen' (Indeed, and I am among those who bear witness) after reciting this verse.
gems.line: Reciters traditionally answer aloud: indeed, and I am of those who bear witness to that.

95:8.morning: The surah closes on a question with one answer - Allah is the most just of judges, whatever today misjudges.
95:8.night: Take the day's unsettled verdicts to the answer - He is the most just of judges, and nothing escaped Him.

2:261.arabic: مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ أَمْوَٰلَهُمْ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ أَنۢبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنَابِلَ فِى كُلِّ سُنۢبُلَةٍۢ مِّا۟ئَةُ حَبَّةٍۢ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ يُضَٰعِفُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ
2:261.translation: The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is that of a grain which grows seven ears, in every ear a hundred grains. Allah enhances severalfold whomever He wishes, and Allah is all-bounteous, all-knowing.

gems.title: Multiplied Reward
gems.insight: Allah multiplies charity up to 700 times or more, transforming a single act into perpetual blessings. Like a seed that produces hundreds of grains, sincere spending in His path yields exponential spiritual returns.
gems.line: Charity multiplies like grain: one act of giving, up to seven hundred returns and counting.

gems.title: Divine Knowledge
gems.insight: Allah knows the intention behind every act of charity and responds with wisdom. His knowledge is vast and encompasses all circumstances, ensuring rewards are distributed with perfect justice.
gems.line: He sees the intention inside each gift; no giving is ever rewarded by its surface alone.

gems.title: Path to Allah
gems.insight: Spending in Allah's way means supporting causes that promote His guidance, justice, and mercy in society. It's not just any charity, but purposeful giving aligned with divine principles.
gems.line: Spending in His way has an aim: giving that carries guidance, justice, and mercy into the world.

gems.title: Seed Parable
gems.insight: The agricultural metaphor reveals divine wisdom: just as farmers trust seeds to multiply through natural law, believers trust Allah's promise to multiply their charity through spiritual law.
gems.line: A farmer buries seed trusting the harvest. Giving rests on the same trust - His promise to multiply.

lines.text: I have submitted to the Lord of all the worlds.
The cow God asked for was free; the cow their questions built cost its weight in gold.
Obedience was always the shortest road; only our questions ever made it long.

2:261.morning: Whatever leaves your hand in His way today is a seed - and He multiplies seeds by the hundred.
2:261.night: Whatever you planted by giving today is now growing in ground you cannot see. Harvest is His promise.

2:263.arabic: ۞ قَوْلٌۭ مَّعْرُوفٌۭ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ خَيْرٌۭ مِّن صَدَقَةٍۢ يَتْبَعُهَآ أَذًۭى ۗ وَٱللَّهُ غَنِىٌّ حَلِيمٌۭ
2:263.translation: An honourable reply [in response to the needy] and forgiving [their annoyance] is better than a charity followed by affront. Allah is all-sufficient, most forbearing.

gems.title: Kind Speech
gems.insight: Gentle words and forgiveness hold greater spiritual value than material charity that humiliates the recipient. Allah elevates dignity-preserving actions over mere financial transactions.
gems.line: Giving that humiliates undoes itself. Kind words that keep a person's dignity rank higher.

gems.title: Self-Sufficient Lord
gems.insight: Allah's complete self-sufficiency means He needs nothing from our charity. His forbearance shows He doesn't punish immediately despite our imperfect giving, granting us time to learn and improve.
gems.line: He needs nothing from your charity - and He is patient with your imperfect giving as you learn.

gems.title: Forgiveness
gems.insight: Pardoning others' faults is ranked alongside kind speech as superior to harmful charity. Forgiveness requires giving up the right to revenge or compensation, a profound internal sacrifice.
gems.line: Forgiving costs from the inside - you surrender your claim - which is why it counts as giving.

lines.text: I have submitted to the Lord of all the worlds.
The cow God asked for was free; the cow their questions built cost its weight in gold.
Obedience was always the shortest road; only our questions ever made it long.

2:263.morning: A kind word today is worth more than an impressive gift that leaves hurt behind.
2:263.night: If all you managed today was kind speech and letting things go, the verse counts it as giving well.

3:92.arabic: لَن تَنَالُوا۟ ٱلْبِرَّ حَتَّىٰ تُنفِقُوا۟ مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ ۚ وَمَا تُنفِقُوا۟ مِن شَىْءٍۢ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِهِۦ عَلِيمٌۭ
3:92.translation: You will never attain piety until you spend out of what you hold dear, and whatever you may spend of anything, Allah indeed knows it.

gems.title: True Righteousness
gems.insight: Attaining al-birr (righteousness and goodness) requires spending from what you truly love and value, not just surplus wealth.
gems.line: Al-birr is not reached from surplus - it begins where the giving starts to cost you something real.

gems.title: Divine Knowledge
gems.insight: Allah has complete knowledge of what we spend and the intentions behind our giving - nothing is hidden from Him.
gems.line: Whatever you give today, and why, is fully known to Him - no gift of yours goes unregistered.

gems.title: Sacrificial Love
gems.insight: The phrase 'from that which you love' indicates that meaningful charity requires giving up things we are attached to, not just excess.
gems.line: 'From what you love' - the attachment is the point. Letting it go is what gives the giving weight.

lines.text: When the truth was put on trial, God reached not for a sword but for a purified family.
One word - purified - travels from Maryam's prayer-niche to the five beneath the cloak.

3:92.morning: Righteousness has a price the verse names plainly: something you love, given while you still love it.
3:92.night: If anything you loved left your hands today, the verse says that is where the good you seek begins.

3:159.arabic: فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍۢ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمْ ۖ وَلَوْ كُنتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ ٱلْقَلْبِ لَٱنفَضُّوا۟ مِنْ حَوْلِكَ ۖ فَٱعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ وَشَاوِرْهُمْ فِى ٱلْأَمْرِ ۖ فَإِذَا عَزَمْتَ فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُتَوَكِّلِينَ
3:159.translation: It is by Allah’s mercy that you are gentle to them; had you been harsh and hardhearted, they would have surely scattered from around you. So excuse them and plead for forgiveness for them, and consult them in the affairs, and once you are resolved, put your trust in Allah. Indeed Allah loves those who trust in Him.

gems.title: Prophetic Mercy
gems.insight: The Prophet's gentle nature came from Allah's mercy, enabling him to be lenient with his companions despite their failures at Uhud.
gems.line: The Prophet's leniency after failure was Allah's mercy in action - softness given, not weakness.

gems.title: Harshness Disperses
gems.insight: If the Prophet had been harsh in speech and hard-hearted, people would have scattered from around him, showing the destructive nature of harshness.
gems.line: Harshness scatters people - even truth, spoken hard-hearted, empties the room around it.

gems.title: Three Commands
gems.insight: After mistakes, the Prophet is commanded to: (1) pardon them, (2) seek forgiveness for them, and (3) consult them in matters.
gems.line: After others' mistakes the sequence is: pardon them, seek forgiveness for them, still consult them.

gems.title: Trust After Decision
gems.insight: After consultation and decision-making, the final step is complete trust (tawakkul) in Allah, showing the balance between human effort and divine reliance.
gems.line: Deliberate, decide, then hand the outcome to Him - tawakkul begins where your part ends.

lines.text: When the truth was put on trial, God reached not for a sword but for a purified family.
One word - purified - travels from Maryam's prayer-niche to the five beneath the cloak.

3:159.morning: The Prophet's gentleness was Allah's mercy at work - gentleness in you today draws from the same source.
3:159.night: Where you chose gentle over harsh today, you kept people near - as mercy kept them near the Prophet.

4:36.arabic: ۞ وَٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُشْرِكُوا۟ بِهِۦ شَيْـًۭٔا ۖ وَبِٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَٰنًۭا وَبِذِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَٱلْيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَٰكِينِ وَٱلْجَارِ ذِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَٱلْجَارِ ٱلْجُنُبِ وَٱلصَّاحِبِ بِٱلْجَنۢبِ وَٱبْنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَمَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُكُمْ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَن كَانَ مُخْتَالًۭا فَخُورًا
4:36.translation: Worship Allah and do not ascribe any partners to Him, and be good to parents, the relatives, the orphans, the needy, the near neighbour and the distant neighbour, the companion at your side, the traveller, and your slaves. Indeed Allah does not like those who are arrogant and boastful.

gems.title: Exclusive Worship
gems.insight: The verse begins with the fundamental command: worship Allah alone without shirk (associating partners). This is the foundation of Islamic monotheism (tawhid).
gems.line: Everything begins at tawhid - worship kept for Him alone is the root the other duties grow from.

gems.title: Circles of Duty
gems.insight: After tawhid, the verse lists seven categories of people deserving good treatment: parents, relatives, orphans, poor, near/far neighbors, companions, travelers, and servants.
gems.line: The verse draws circles around you - parents, kin, orphans, neighbors, travelers - each owed good.

gems.title: Neighbor's Rights
gems.insight: Islam distinguishes between the near neighbor (dhi al-qurba) and distant neighbor (al-janub), showing concern for both close and distant community members.
gems.line: Near neighbor and far neighbor are both named - proximity is not the boundary of your care.

gems.title: Rejecting Arrogance
gems.insight: Allah does not love those who are mukhtal (self-deluded/arrogant) and fakhur (boastful). Pride prevents fulfilling social duties and seeing others as worthy of kindness.
gems.line: The verse ends warning against arrogance - pride closes the hand that duty needs open.

lines.text: Taste this, Ali - taste the fire. This is for the one who fails the widow and the orphan.
A right on a page protects no one; every right is a trust placed in someone's hands.
Obedience closes the distance that love alone cannot close.

4:36.morning: The verse orders the day: worship belonging to Him alone, then goodness flowing outward to kin and neighbor.
4:36.night: Worship of Him and goodness to those around you sat in one verse today - the near, the far, all inside it.

4:86.arabic: وَإِذَا حُيِّيتُم بِتَحِيَّةٍۢ فَحَيُّوا۟ بِأَحْسَنَ مِنْهَآ أَوْ رُدُّوهَآ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ حَسِيبًا
4:86.translation: When you are greeted with a salute, greet with a better one than it, or return it; indeed Allah takes account of all things.

gems.title: Better Greeting
gems.insight: When greeted, respond with a better greeting or at least equal. This establishes a culture of escalating kindness and courtesy in Muslim interactions.
gems.line: Answering a greeting with a better one turns ordinary hellos into escalating kindness.

gems.title: Islamic Manners
gems.insight: This verse establishes formal etiquette for greetings. Islam cares about the details of human interaction, recognizing that small courtesies build strong communities.
gems.line: He legislated the small courtesies too - the details of how you greet people matter to Him.

gems.title: Reckoning of All
gems.insight: The verse ends stating Allah is Hasib - an Accountant over all things. Even something as small as a greeting is noted and will be accounted for.
gems.line: Even a greeting sits in His account - nothing you exchange today is too small to be counted.

lines.text: Taste this, Ali - taste the fire. This is for the one who fails the widow and the orphan.
A right on a page protects no one; every right is a trust placed in someone's hands.
Obedience closes the distance that love alone cannot close.

4:86.morning: Every greeting that reaches you today invites a better one back - kindness is meant to escalate.
4:86.night: The small courtesies you gave today were not lost - He is an Accountant over even a greeting.

4:149.arabic: إِن تُبْدُوا۟ خَيْرًا أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ أَوْ تَعْفُوا۟ عَن سُوٓءٍۢ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَفُوًّۭا قَدِيرًا
4:149.translation: Whether you disclose a good [deed that you do] or hide it, or excuse an evil [deed], Allah is indeed all-excusing, all-powerful.

gems.title: Public Goodness
gems.insight: Whether you reveal good deeds (tubdu khayran) or conceal them, both approaches have merit. Public good can inspire others, while private good protects from showing off.
gems.line: Good shown can inspire; good hidden stays safe from show - the verse honors both ways of giving.

gems.title: Gracious Forgiveness
gems.insight: The verse especially highlights pardoning evil (ta'fu 'an su'), encouraging believers to overlook offenses and forgive wrongs. This reflects divine mercy in human interactions.
gems.line: Overlooking an offense is divine mercy practiced at human scale.

gems.title: The Great Pardoner
gems.insight: Allah describes Himself as 'Afuwwan (Ever-Pardoning), one who completely erases sins as if they never happened. This goes beyond forgiveness to total erasure of wrongdoing.
gems.line: Afuww is His name - not just forgiving a wrong but erasing it as if it never was.

gems.title: Absolute Power
gems.insight: The verse concludes with Qadir (Competent/Powerful), reminding that Allah's pardon comes from strength, not weakness. He has full power to punish yet chooses mercy.
gems.line: His pardon comes from full power to do otherwise - mercy chosen from strength, never weakness.

lines.text: Taste this, Ali - taste the fire. This is for the one who fails the widow and the orphan.
A right on a page protects no one; every right is a trust placed in someone's hands.
Obedience closes the distance that love alone cannot close.

4:149.morning: Pardoning an offense today puts you on His pattern - He is Ever-Pardoning, and pardons from power.
4:149.night: If you let an offense go today, you mirrored the strong kind of mercy - His pardon comes from power.

7:199.arabic: خُذِ ٱلْعَفْوَ وَأْمُرْ بِٱلْعُرْفِ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ ٱلْجَٰهِلِينَ
7:199.translation: Adopt [a policy of] excusing [the faults of people], bid what is right, and turn away from the ignorant.

gems.title: Accept Easiness
gems.insight: The command 'take what is given freely' (خُذِ ٱلْعَفْوَ) instructs the Prophet to accept people's natural ease, not demanding perfection. Al-'afw means pardoning and accepting what people offer without burden.
gems.line: What people offer freely, accepted without demanding more - that is the verse's first command.

gems.title: Command Virtue
gems.insight: The verse commands 'enjoin what is good' (وَأْمُرْ بِٱلْعُرْفِ) - actively promoting recognized virtue and goodness. This is the responsibility of all believers, especially leaders, to guide others toward righteousness.
gems.line: Goodness is not only practiced but urged - promoting what is right is part of carrying this faith.

gems.title: Turn From Ignorance
gems.insight: The instruction to 'turn away from the ignorant' (وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ ٱلْجَٰهِلِينَ) teaches strategic disengagement from those who persistently reject guidance with arrogance and mockery.
gems.line: Not every argument deserves you - turning from entrenched mockery is wisdom, not weakness.

gems.title: Noble Character
gems.insight: These three qualities - accepting ease, commanding good, and avoiding ignorant arguments - form the core of prophetic character: gentleness combined with moral courage and wise discretion.
gems.line: Gentleness, moral courage, knowing when to walk away - one verse holds the Prophet's character.

lines.text: You said yes once, before you can remember; your life is the second time you are asked.
They walked in as Pharaoh's hired magicians at sunrise; before sunset they were martyrs.
Pride, heedlessness, or a slow letting-go: every fall in al-A'raf is one promise slipping.

7:199.morning: One verse can run a whole day: take what comes easily, urge what is good, turn from the ignorant.
7:199.night: Tonight's measure is one verse: what you accepted with ease, the good you urged, the arguments you left.

9:103.arabic: خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَٰلِهِمْ صَدَقَةًۭ تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِم بِهَا وَصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ ۖ إِنَّ صَلَوٰتَكَ سَكَنٌۭ لَّهُمْ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
9:103.translation: Take charity from their possessions to cleanse them and purify them thereby, and bless them. Indeed your blessing is a comfort to them, and Allah is all-hearing, all-knowing.

gems.title: Purifying Charity
gems.insight: 'Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them' - sadaqah cleanses both wealth and soul, removing the spiritual contamination of sin.
gems.line: Charity is hygiene for the soul - what leaves your hand takes some of the heart's residue along.

gems.title: Cause Increase
gems.insight: 'And cause them increase' (tuzakkihim) - charity doesn't diminish wealth but increases it, both materially through barakah and spiritually through purification.
gems.line: Giving runs against arithmetic - wealth given grows, in barakah outside and in purity within.

gems.title: Prophet's Prayers
gems.insight: 'Invoke Allah's blessings upon them. Indeed, your invocations are reassurance for them' - the Prophet's prayers bring peace and comfort to troubled souls.
gems.line: The givers received the Prophet's prayer - and his prayer, the verse says, is rest for their souls.

gems.title: Hearing & Knowing
gems.insight: 'Allah is Hearing and Knowing' - He hears every prayer and knows every intention behind charity, rewarding based on complete knowledge.
gems.line: He hears the prayer over your gift and knows the intention in it - reward follows the full truth.

lines.text: Before you ever turned toward God, He had already turned toward you.
The one who repents of a sin is as one with no sin at all.
Every road away from God turns, and leads back into His mercy.

9:103.morning: What you give today does double work the verse describes: it purifies you, and it makes you grow.
9:103.night: If charity left your hands today, it did not simply leave - it purified, and set growth in motion.

9:119.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَكُونُوا۟ مَعَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
9:119.translation: O you who have faith! Be wary of Allah, and be with the Truthful.

gems.title: Conscious Awareness
gems.insight: The command 'fear Allah' (اتقوا الله) calls for taqwa - God-consciousness that makes us mindful of His presence in every action. It's not terror but reverent awareness.
gems.line: Taqwa is not terror - it is moving through the day aware that He is present in every action.

gems.title: Righteous Company
gems.insight: Believers are commanded to 'be with the truthful' (كونوا مع الصادقين) - associating with those of genuine faith and integrity. Spiritual companionship shapes character.
gems.line: 'Be with the truthful' makes companionship a command - who you stand with shapes who you become.

gems.title: Dual Imperative
gems.insight: The verse gives two interconnected commands: cultivate God-consciousness (taqwa) and seek righteous companionship. Internal piety and external community work together.
gems.line: God-consciousness within and good company around come as one instruction - each guards the other.

lines.text: Before you ever turned toward God, He had already turned toward you.
The one who repents of a sin is as one with no sin at all.
Every road away from God turns, and leads back into His mercy.

9:119.morning: Two commands shape today: keep taqwa of Allah, and keep the truthful within your company.
9:119.night: The day ends where it began: with Him held in awareness, and the truthful counted as your people.

14:31.arabic: قُل لِّعِبَادِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ يُقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَيُنفِقُوا۟ مِمَّا رَزَقْنَٰهُمْ سِرًّۭا وَعَلَانِيَةًۭ مِّن قَبْلِ أَن يَأْتِىَ يَوْمٌۭ لَّا بَيْعٌۭ فِيهِ وَلَا خِلَٰلٌ
14:31.translation: Tell My servants who have faith to maintain the prayer and to spend out of what We have provided them with, secretly and openly, before there comes a day on which there will be neither any bargaining nor friendship.

gems.title: Prayer & Charity
gems.insight: The verse pairs salah (prayer) with spending from Allah's provision, showing worship encompasses both spiritual devotion and social responsibility.
gems.line: Salah and spending stand side by side - devotion to Him and duty to people form one worship.

gems.title: Hidden & Open Giving
gems.insight: Allah commands giving both secretly (preserving dignity) and publicly (inspiring others) - each form serves a divine purpose.
gems.line: Secret giving guards dignity; open giving inspires others - both forms carry divine purpose.

gems.title: No Bargaining Day
gems.insight: The Day of Judgment will have no trade, no ransom, no friendships that can save - only deeds and Allah's mercy matter.
gems.line: A Day is coming with no trade and no ransom - what is given now is given while giving still counts.

lines.text: A good word is like a good tree: its root is firm, and its branch reaches into the sky.
I am the prayer of my father Ibrahim.
What is planted with God in dead ground is never wasted; it grows while you are gone.

14:31.morning: Prayer and giving belong to today - the verse points to a Day when no trade or friendship can be offered.
14:31.night: What you prayed and gave today went ahead of you - to a Day with no trade and no friendships to lean on.

16:91.arabic: وَأَوْفُوا۟ بِعَهْدِ ٱللَّهِ إِذَا عَٰهَدتُّمْ وَلَا تَنقُضُوا۟ ٱلْأَيْمَٰنَ بَعْدَ تَوْكِيدِهَا وَقَدْ جَعَلْتُمُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَيْكُمْ كَفِيلًا ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ
16:91.translation: Fulfill Allah’s covenant when you pledge, and do not break [your] oaths, after pledging them solemnly and having made Allah a witness over yourselves. Indeed Allah knows what you do.

gems.title: Sacred Covenant
gems.insight: Fulfilling Allah's covenant is not optional - it's a binding commitment witnessed by Allah Himself. Breaking oaths after confirmation violates divine trust.
gems.line: A confirmed oath is not paperwork - it is a trust with Allah Himself standing surety over it.

gems.title: Allah as Witness
gems.insight: When we make oaths, we invoke Allah as our witness. He is not a passive observer - He knows every action and intention behind our commitments.
gems.line: The One you invoked as witness is not passive - He knows the intention behind every commitment.

gems.title: All-Knowing
gems.insight: Allah's knowledge encompasses not just what we say, but what we do. There's no hiding broken promises or hollow commitments from His perfect awareness.
gems.line: Kept or broken, your word sits in His full view - He knows what you do with every promise.

lines.text: They recognize the blessing of Allah - then they deny it.
Asked what a good life means in the Qur'an, he said: it is contentment.
The surah is named not for the pouring, but for the one who received it rightly.

16:91.morning: Every promise you make today gains a witness at once - you place Allah as guarantor over your word.
16:91.night: The promises still standing tonight are still witnessed - Allah knows what you do with each one.

16:125.arabic: ٱدْعُ إِلَىٰ سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ بِٱلْحِكْمَةِ وَٱلْمَوْعِظَةِ ٱلْحَسَنَةِ ۖ وَجَٰدِلْهُم بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ ۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ ۖ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِٱلْمُهْتَدِينَ
16:125.translation: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good advice and dispute with them in a manner that is best. Indeed your Lord knows best those who stray from His way, and He knows best those who are guided.

gems.title: Wisdom in Da'wah
gems.insight: 'Hikmah' (wisdom) means choosing the right message, right method, and right timing for each audience. Effective da'wah requires reading people's hearts, not just reciting scripture.
gems.line: Wisdom reads the person in front of you - right message, right method, right moment for this heart.

gems.title: Beautiful Instruction
gems.insight: 'Maw'izah hasanah' (beautiful preaching) means presenting Islam's guidance in attractive, compassionate ways that touch hearts. Truth delivered beautifully penetrates defenses.
gems.line: Truth delivered beautifully gets past defenses - compassion is part of the message, not decoration.

gems.title: Gracious Debate
gems.insight: 'Argue with them in the best way' means engaging doubts and questions with respect, not defensiveness. Even when challenged, respond with the most gracious, compelling arguments.
gems.line: Met with challenge, the standard stays - the best argument, offered with respect intact.

gems.title: Divine Knowledge
gems.insight: Allah knows best who is misguided and who is guided. This removes the burden of converting people from us - our job is invitation, Allah's job is guidance.
gems.line: Guidance is His work, not yours - your part ends at the invitation, and that lifts the weight.

lines.text: They recognize the blessing of Allah - then they deny it.
Asked what a good life means in the Qur'an, he said: it is contentment.
The surah is named not for the pouring, but for the one who received it rightly.

16:125.morning: Truth travels on manner - wisdom, beauty, and grace are how the way of your Lord is offered to anyone.
16:125.night: Every word of truth you offered today was the whole of your job - who it guides rests with your Lord.

17:28.arabic: وَإِمَّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ ٱبْتِغَآءَ رَحْمَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّكَ تَرْجُوهَا فَقُل لَّهُمْ قَوْلًۭا مَّيْسُورًۭا
17:28.translation: And if you have to hold off from [assisting] them [for now], seeking your Lord’s mercy which you expect [in the future], speak to them gentle words.

gems.title: Temporary Inability
gems.insight: The verse addresses those who must 'turn away from the needy awaiting mercy from your Lord' (تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ ٱبْتِغَآءَ رَحْمَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّكَ تَرْجُوهَا) due to current poverty. Even when unable to give financially, believers must maintain dignity and kindness in refusal.
gems.line: An empty hand does not excuse a hard face - dignity is owed even in refusal.

gems.title: Kind Refusal
gems.insight: The command 'speak to them a gentle word' (فَقُل لَّهُمْ قَوْلًۭا مَّيْسُورًۭا) when unable to help financially shows Islam's attention to psychological and emotional care. Maysooran implies ease, softness - words that don't compound the seeker's hardship with humiliation.
gems.line: A gentle word spares the asker humiliation - softness stands in where money is missing.

gems.title: Hopeful Waiting
gems.insight: The phrase 'awaiting mercy from your Lord which you expect' (ٱبْتِغَآءَ رَحْمَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّكَ تَرْجُوهَا) acknowledges that current inability is temporary. The poor person today may have resources tomorrow - provision comes from Allah's ongoing mercy, not static circumstances.
gems.line: Today's inability is not permanent - provision moves by His mercy, and tomorrow can open.

gems.title: Beyond Money
gems.insight: This verse expands charity beyond financial giving. When material aid is impossible, we offer emotional support, respectful speech, genuine empathy, and prayer. These non-monetary forms of sadaqah maintain social bonds and human dignity.
gems.line: Charity is wider than money - respect, empathy, and prayer are giving your hand can always afford.

17:28.morning: Even a day with nothing to give still leaves something to offer - a gentle word is within reach.
17:28.night: The gentle words you managed today counted as giving - charity never depended on your wallet.

17:29.arabic: وَلَا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلَىٰ عُنُقِكَ وَلَا تَبْسُطْهَا كُلَّ ٱلْبَسْطِ فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُومًۭا مَّحْسُورًا
17:29.translation: Do not keep your hand chained to your neck, nor open it altogether, or you will sit blameworthy and regretful.

gems.title: Balanced Hands
gems.insight: The vivid imagery 'do not make your hand chained to your neck' (وَلَا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلَىٰ عُنُقِكَ) depicts miserliness - being so tight-fisted one cannot give. Conversely, 'nor extend it completely' (وَلَا تَبْسُطْهَا كُلَّ ٱلْبَسْطِ) warns against reckless generosity that leaves one destitute.
gems.line: Neither chained to your neck nor opened to the last coin - the hand is meant to move with measure.

gems.title: Double Consequence
gems.insight: The dual outcome 'become blamed and insolvent' (فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُومًۭا مَّحْسُورًا) shows consequences of financial extremes. Maloom (blamed) indicates social/moral reproach, while mahsoor (insolvent/regretful) points to practical destitution and psychological distress.
gems.line: Both extremes charge twice - blame from people and depletion within. Balance spares you both.

gems.title: Middle Path
gems.insight: This verse embodies the Islamic principle of wasatiyyah (moderation). Between the extremes of miserliness and recklessness lies the balanced path: generous enough to fulfill obligations and help others, prudent enough to ensure future stability.
gems.line: Moderation is the path itself - generous enough to lift others, prudent enough to stand tomorrow.

gems.title: Wise Generosity
gems.insight: Shia scholars emphasize sustainable charity that doesn't deplete resources. The goal is creating ongoing capacity to help, not one-time gestures that leave us unable to assist in the future. This requires strategic thinking about wealth and giving.
gems.line: Giving that lasts beats giving that empties - sustained capacity to help is the wiser generosity.

17:29.morning: Two extremes are named and closed - a hand chained shut and a hand emptied out. Today walks between them.
17:29.night: If your hand moved with measure today, it ends the day neither chained nor bare - the balance held.

17:37.arabic: وَلَا تَمْشِ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مَرَحًا ۖ إِنَّكَ لَن تَخْرِقَ ٱلْأَرْضَ وَلَن تَبْلُغَ ٱلْجِبَالَ طُولًۭا
17:37.translation: Do not walk exultantly on the earth. Indeed, you will neither pierce the earth, nor reach the mountains in height.

gems.title: Walking Humbly
gems.insight: The prohibition against walking 'exultantly' (marahan) addresses arrogance expressed through physical bearing. How we carry ourselves reveals internal pride or humility.
gems.line: Pride leaks into posture - humility is carried in the body, not only held in the heart.

gems.title: Human Limitations
gems.insight: The verse reminds us 'you will never tear the earth apart, and you will never reach the mountains in height' - powerful imagery showing human powerlessness before creation.
gems.line: You will not split the earth or match the mountains - creation's scale keeps you honestly sized.

gems.title: Rejecting Pride
gems.insight: By linking physical arrogance to cosmic impossibility, the verse teaches that pride is fundamentally irrational - we have nothing to be arrogant about given our inherent weakness.
gems.line: Arrogance fails arithmetic - beside your actual power, pride has nothing to stand on.

17:37.morning: Humility has a gait - the verse reads arrogance in a walk before it ever reaches words.
17:37.night: The earth you walked today outlasts every proud stride - the gentle walk was the truthful one.

24:27.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَدْخُلُوا۟ بُيُوتًا غَيْرَ بُيُوتِكُمْ حَتَّىٰ تَسْتَأْنِسُوا۟ وَتُسَلِّمُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهَا ۚ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌۭ لَّكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ
24:27.translation: O you who have faith! Do not enter houses other than your own until you have announced [your arrival] and greeted their occupants. That is better for you. Maybe you will take admonition.

gems.title: Respect Privacy
gems.insight: Believers must seek permission (istinas) before entering others' homes and offer greetings of peace (taslim). This establishes divine protocol for respecting privacy and domestic sanctity.
gems.line: Privacy carries divine protection - a home's threshold is honored before it is crossed.

gems.title: Sacred Greeting
gems.insight: Offering 'salam' is not mere social formality but recognition of the spiritual bond between believers, invoking Allah's mercy upon one another.
gems.line: Salam is more than politeness - it invokes His mercy and names the bond between believers.

gems.title: Spiritual Benefit
gems.insight: The phrase 'that is best for you' indicates this etiquette brings spiritual benefit beyond social courtesy—cultivating taqwa (God-consciousness) through interpersonal ethics.
gems.line: 'That is best for you' - etiquette at the door is counted toward taqwa, not mere manners.

gems.title: Divine Reminder
gems.insight: The verse ends with 'perhaps you will be reminded' (la'allakum tadhakkarun), inviting reflection on the wisdom of divine ordinances that protect both individual and communal wellbeing.
gems.line: The closing invites reflection - His ordinances guard the person and the community at once.

24:27.morning: Today's courtesy is revealed, not invented: seek welcome, greet with peace, and then enter.
