gems.insight: True believers strive with their wealth in Allah's path, showing that genuine faith manifests in financial sacrifice and generosity for the cause.
gems.line: What genuine faith holds, it spends - wealth given in His path is belief made visible.

gems.title: Physical Sacrifice
gems.insight: True believers strive with their lives/selves, indicating that genuine faith requires personal effort, physical sacrifice, and putting oneself at risk for the cause.
gems.line: The striving includes the self - person and effort placed where the wealth already went.

gems.title: Truly Truthful
gems.insight: Those with unwavering faith who strive with wealth and life are declared 'the truthful,' showing that actions validate claims of belief.
gems.line: 'It is those who are the truthful' - the claim of faith is proven by what it has given.

49:15.morning: The verse defines the truthful: belief without wavering, then wealth and self given in His path.
49:15.night: By this verse the truthful are known not by words but by what they staked - faith, wealth, and self.

94:7.translation: So when you are done, appoint,

gems.title: After Completion
gems.insight: 'Fa-idha faraghta' (when you have finished) refers to completing one duty before moving to the next - finish your worldly obligations, then turn fully to worship without distraction.
gems.line: Faraghta marks a completion - when duty is done, devotion is what the freed hours are for.

gems.title: Stand in Worship
gems.insight: 'Fansab' (stand up/exert effort) implies active, effortful worship - not passive leisure but intentional spiritual labor even when worldly work is done.
gems.line: Fansab asks for exertion - worship offered with effort, not the leftovers of a tired evening.

gems.title: Continuous Service
gems.insight: The verse establishes rhythm: worldly duty → spiritual devotion → worldly duty → spiritual devotion. Life is continuous service to Allah in alternating forms.
gems.line: Work, then worship, then work again - the verse sets a rhythm where all of it is service to Him.

94:7.morning: The day's tasks come with a sequel - when one work is finished, the verse appoints the next: stand for Him.
94:7.night: If the day's work is finished, the verse's moment is now - what follows completion is devotion.

3:169.arabic: وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَمْوَٰتًۢا ۚ بَلْ أَحْيَآءٌ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ يُرْزَقُونَ
3:169.translation: Do not suppose those who were slain in the way of Allah to be dead; no, they are living and provided for near their Lord,

gems.title: Living Martyrs
gems.insight: Those killed in Allah's cause are not dead but alive with their Lord, receiving provision. Martyrdom is not an ending but a transition to a higher form of life.
gems.line: Martyrdom is not an ending - it is passage into a higher life, alive with their Lord.

gems.title: Eternal Provision
gems.insight: The martyrs receive continuous provision from Allah. Their sustenance does not cease with physical death but continues in a superior realm.
gems.line: Their provision never stopped - sustenance continues with their Lord, in a realm above this one.

gems.title: Perception Shift
gems.insight: Allah commands us not to think of martyrs as dead - a direct correction of how we perceive those who die in His cause. Our earthly perspective needs divine adjustment.
gems.line: The verse corrects the eye - what grief sees as an ending, He declares to be life.

lines.text: When the truth was put on trial, God reached not for a sword but for a purified family.
One word - purified - travels from Maryam's prayer-niche to the five beneath the cloak.

3:169.morning: It is Ashura. Over Karbala this verse stands guard: the ones killed in His cause are alive with their Lord.
3:169.night: Ashura closes. The mourned of Karbala are not gone - alive with their Lord, receiving provision.

22:27.arabic: وَأَذِّن فِى ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلْحَجِّ يَأْتُوكَ رِجَالًۭا وَعَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرٍۢ يَأْتِينَ مِن كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍۢ
22:27.translation: And proclaim the Hajj to all the people: they will come to you on foot and on lean camels, coming from distant places,

gems.title: Proclamation to All
gems.insight: Allah commanded Ibrahim to proclaim Hajj to all people - a universal invitation transcending geography, ethnicity, and time.
gems.line: One man was told to proclaim, and the call outlived him - an invitation without border or era.

gems.title: Journey of Faith
gems.insight: Pilgrims will come on foot and on lean camels from every distant pass - the difficulty of the journey purifies intention and increases reward.
gems.line: The hard road is part of the worship - distance walked for Him purifies intention, lifts reward.

gems.title: Promised Response
gems.insight: The verse states 'they will come to you' with certainty - Allah guarantees that His call through Ibrahim will be answered across all time.
gems.line: 'They will come' is stated as certainty - the call placed on Ibrahim's lips is still answered.

22:27.morning: It is Arbaeen. The verse's image is alive today: pilgrims on foot, arriving from every distant pass.
22:27.night: Arbaeen closes. Walkers filled the roads again today, and the verse's image was easy to believe.

3:144.arabic: وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌۭ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُ ۚ أَفَإِي۟ن مَّاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ ٱنقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَعْقَٰبِكُمْ ۚ وَمَن يَنقَلِبْ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ فَلَن يَضُرَّ ٱللَّهَ شَيْـًۭٔا ۗ وَسَيَجْزِى ٱللَّهُ ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
3:144.translation: Muhammad is but an apostle; [other] apostles have passed before him. If he dies or is slain, will you turn back on your heels? Anyone who turns back on his heels, will not harm Allah in the least, and soon Allah will reward the grateful.

gems.title: Prophet's Mortality
gems.insight: Allah explicitly declares that Muhammad is only a messenger and will die or be killed like all prophets before him. This establishes that even the Prophet is subject to natural law and mortality.
gems.line: The message was built to outlast the messenger - faith stands on the One who sent him.

gems.title: Apostasy Warning
gems.insight: Allah questions whether believers would abandon faith if the Prophet died or was killed. This addresses the rumor at Uhud that the Prophet was killed, which caused some to waver or flee.
gems.line: At Uhud a rumor tested where faith was anchored - anchored in Allah, it does not turn on its heels.

gems.title: Divine Independence
gems.insight: The verse states that those who turn back from faith cannot harm Allah at all. This establishes Allah's complete independence from creation - our faith benefits us, not Him.
gems.line: Turning back harms Allah nothing at all - faith was always for your benefit, never His need.

gems.title: Reward for Gratitude
gems.insight: Allah promises to reward those who remain grateful and steadfast even when facing the loss of beloved leaders. Gratitude here means maintaining faith despite grief and adversity.
gems.line: The grateful here are those who keep faith through grief - and Allah Himself promises their reward.

lines.text: When the truth was put on trial, God reached not for a sword but for a purified family.
One word - purified - travels from Maryam's prayer-niche to the five beneath the cloak.

3:144.morning: On the day the ummah lost the Prophet, this verse held it steady: faith rests on his Lord, who remains.
3:144.night: The day of the Prophet's departure closes as the verse taught: grief held with gratitude, faith standing.

21:107.translation: We did not send you but as a mercy to all the nations.

gems.title: Universal Mercy
gems.insight: The Prophet Muhammad is described as 'rahma lil-alamin' - a mercy to all the worlds. This encompasses not just Muslims but all of humanity, creation, and even the spiritual realms.
gems.line: Rahma lil-alamin - his mercy reaches all humanity and creation, not one community alone.

gems.title: Prophetic Purpose
gems.insight: The exclusive particle 'illa' (except/only) emphasizes that the Prophet's entire mission can be summed up in one word: mercy. Every aspect of his teachings, actions, and guidance serves this purpose.
gems.line: One word holds his whole mission - 'only as a mercy' - every teaching of his serves it.

gems.title: Divine Commission
gems.insight: The verb 'arsalnaka' (We sent you) emphasizes divine authority and commission. The Prophet didn't appoint himself but was chosen and sent by Allah with a specific mission.
gems.line: 'We sent you' - the Prophet was commissioned by Allah Himself, chosen and sent with purpose.

gems.title: Cosmic Scope
gems.insight: The plural 'alamin' (worlds) indicates the vast scope of the prophetic mercy - extending to all creation including humans, jinn, animals, and even the environment.
gems.line: 'The worlds' is deliberately plural - humans, jinn, animals, the earth itself, all within it.

21:107.morning: It is the Mawlid - the day opens on his description: not sent except as a mercy to the worlds.
21:107.night: The Mawlid closes with the verse still true: he was sent as a mercy to the worlds - yours among them.

33:33.arabic: وَقَرْنَ فِى بُيُوتِكُنَّ وَلَا تَبَرَّجْنَ تَبَرُّجَ ٱلْجَٰهِلِيَّةِ ٱلْأُولَىٰ ۖ وَأَقِمْنَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتِينَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَطِعْنَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥٓ ۚ إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيُذْهِبَ عَنكُمُ ٱلرِّجْسَ أَهْلَ ٱلْبَيْتِ وَيُطَهِّرَكُمْ تَطْهِيرًۭا
33:33.translation: Stay in your houses and do not flaunt your finery like the former [days of pagan] ignorance. Maintain the prayer and pay the zakat, and obey Allah and His Apostle. Indeed Allah desires to repel all impurity from you, O People of the Household, and purify you with a thorough purification.

gems.title: Domestic Dignity
gems.insight: The instruction to 'settle in your homes' establishes the home as a place of honor and spiritual cultivation, not confinement but dignified presence.
gems.line: The home in the verse is a place of honor and cultivation - dignified presence, not confinement.

gems.title: Purification Verse
gems.insight: The famous 'Ayat al-Tathir' declares Allah's will to remove impurity from the 'Ahlul Bayt' (People of the House) and purify them completely - a foundational verse in Shia theology.
gems.line: Ayat al-Tathir states His will: impurity removed from the Ahlul Bayt, purification complete.

gems.title: Ahlul Bayt
gems.insight: The term 'Ahlul Bayt' (People of the House) specifically designates the Prophet's closest family members as holders of special spiritual status and divine protection.
gems.line: 'People of the House' is a designation, not a description - the Prophet's nearest, in special rank.

gems.title: Abandon Jahiliyyah
gems.insight: The prohibition against displaying oneself 'as in the former times of ignorance' (Jahiliyyah) calls for abandoning pre-Islamic practices that objectified women.
gems.line: The verse turns from Jahiliyyah's display - the old ignorance that reduced women is left behind.

33:33.morning: It is the martyrdom of Sayyida Fatima - the verse of purification stands over her house today.
33:33.night: The night of Sayyida Fatima's martyrdom closes under the verse's word for her house: purified, completely.

2:207.arabic: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشْرِى نَفْسَهُ ٱبْتِغَآءَ مَرْضَاتِ ٱللَّهِ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ رَءُوفٌۢ بِٱلْعِبَادِ
2:207.translation: And among the people is he who sells his soul seeking the pleasure of Allah, and Allah is most kind to [His] servants.

gems.title: Ultimate Sacrifice
gems.insight: In contrast to the arrogant hypocrite, some believers 'sell themselves' - dedicating their entire existence to seeking Allah's pleasure and approval.
gems.line: There is a kind of person who holds nothing back - a whole life traded for His pleasure alone.

gems.title: Allah's Kindness
gems.insight: The verse concludes affirming that Allah is 'Ra'uf' (extremely kind) to His servants - reassuring those who sacrifice for Him that His mercy exceeds their efforts.
gems.line: Whoever gives everything for Him finds His kindness was already larger than the sacrifice.

gems.title: Martyrdom Spirit
gems.insight: This verse is often understood to reference those who sacrificed their lives for Islam, including companions who gave everything for the faith.
gems.line: Some gave their very lives for this faith. The verse keeps their trade from being forgotten.

lines.text: I have submitted to the Lord of all the worlds.
The cow God asked for was free; the cow their questions built cost its weight in gold.
Obedience was always the shortest road; only our questions ever made it long.

2:207.morning: On the day Imam Ali was born, the verse honors the one who sells his whole self for God's pleasure.
2:207.night: The birthday of Imam Ali closes - a life spent for God's pleasure, met by a Lord kind to His servants.

96:1.arabic: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ
96:1.translation: Read in the Name of your Lord who created;

gems.title: Recite
gems.insight: Iqra' (recite/read) is the first divine command of revelation, marking the beginning of the Quran's descent and emphasizing knowledge as Islam's foundation.
gems.line: Iqra' came first - revelation opened with a command to read, setting knowledge at the foundation.

gems.title: In Your Lord's Name
gems.insight: Reading 'in the name of your Lord' sanctifies knowledge - all learning must begin with acknowledging Allah as the source of wisdom and truth.
gems.line: Learning begins 'in the name of your Lord' - knowledge is sanctified by naming its true source.

gems.title: The Creator
gems.insight: Allathee khalaq (who created) immediately connects reading and knowledge to Allah's creative power - studying creation reveals the Creator.
gems.line: The Lord who commands reading is the One who created - creation, read closely, shows its Maker.

96:1.morning: On Mab'ath the first revealed word returns to its day: iqra' - read, in the name of your Lord who created.
96:1.night: Mab'ath ends - the day that honors revelation's first word, iqra', and all the guidance that followed.

42:23.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ ٱلَّذِى يُبَشِّرُ ٱللَّهُ عِبَادَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ ۗ قُل لَّآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْرًا إِلَّا ٱلْمَوَدَّةَ فِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ ۗ وَمَن يَقْتَرِفْ حَسَنَةًۭ نَّزِدْ لَهُۥ فِيهَا حُسْنًا ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌۭ شَكُورٌ
42:23.translation: Such is the good news that Allah gives to His servants who have faith and do righteous deeds! Say, ‘I do not ask you any reward for it except the love of [my] relatives.’ Whoever performs a good deed, We shall enhance its goodness for him. Indeed Allah is all-forgiving, all-appreciative.

gems.title: Love of Kinship
gems.insight: The Prophet asks for no payment except 'love for those of kinship' (mawaddah fi'l-qurba), which Shia scholars understand as love for the Ahlul Bayt, the Prophet's family.
gems.line: The one wage asked is mawaddah fi'l-qurba - in Shia understanding, love for the Ahlul Bayt.

gems.title: No Worldly Wage
gems.insight: The Prophet declares he seeks no worldly payment for delivering Allah's message, establishing that spiritual guidance should be freely given, not commercialized.
gems.line: The Prophet took no worldly payment for the message - guidance is given freely, never sold.

gems.title: Increased Goodness
gems.insight: Whoever commits a good deed, Allah will increase its goodness for them, showing divine generosity that multiplies rewards far beyond our meager efforts.
gems.line: Whoever earns one good deed finds its goodness increased - His return outgrows your effort.

gems.title: Forgiving & Appreciative
gems.insight: Allah is Ghafur (Forgiving) and Shakur (Appreciative) - He forgives our sins and deeply appreciates even small good deeds, a perfect combination of mercy and recognition.
gems.line: Ghafur and Shakur - He forgives what went wrong and treasures even the smallest good you did.

42:23.morning: On the birth of Imam Husayn, the verse's asked-for wage has a face: love for the Prophet's near kin.
42:23.night: The child born on this night is, in Shia reading, of the qurba named here - love the one wage asked.

28:5.arabic: وَنُرِيدُ أَن نَّمُنَّ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتُضْعِفُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَنَجْعَلَهُمْ أَئِمَّةًۭ وَنَجْعَلَهُمُ ٱلْوَٰرِثِينَ
28:5.translation: And We desired to show favour to those who were abased in the land, and to make them imams, and to make them the heirs,

gems.title: Divine Favor
gems.insight: Allah declares His will to elevate the oppressed as leaders and inheritors, transcending material power to focus on spiritual authority rooted in divine guidance.
gems.line: The lifting of the oppressed is His declared will - authority rooted in guidance, not brute power.

gems.title: Divine Leadership
gems.insight: Making the oppressed 'leaders' (a'imma) connects to Shia understanding of Imamate, wherein true leadership emerges from divine designation, not temporal power.
gems.line: The oppressed are made a'imma, leaders - in Shia understanding, leadership is designated by Allah.

gems.title: Final Victory
gems.insight: Shia scholars link this verse to the Mahdi's reappearance, wherein the oppressed will assume global leadership, fulfilling Allah's eternal covenant.
gems.line: Shia scholars read here the Mahdi's return - the oppressed will lead, and the earth is inherited.

28:5.morning: On the birth of Imam al-Mahdi, the verse's promise has a face: the oppressed made leaders and heirs.
28:5.night: The night of his birth holds the verse's assurance: Allah still intends the oppressed to inherit.

2:183.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ
2:183.translation: O you who have faith! Prescribed for you is fasting as it was prescribed for those who were before you, so that you may be Godwary.

gems.title: Fasting Obligation
gems.insight: Fasting (siyam) is prescribed (kutiba) just as it was for previous communities. This universal practice connects Muslims to a long prophetic tradition of spiritual discipline.
gems.line: This fast is older than you: prophets and their peoples carried it before it reached your hands.

gems.title: Gateway to Taqwa
gems.insight: The purpose of fasting is 'la'allakum tattaqun' - that you may attain taqwa (God-consciousness). Hunger and thirst train the soul to prioritize spiritual over physical needs.
gems.line: The fast's goal is not hunger but taqwa - the body steps back so awareness of Him steps forward.

gems.title: Prophetic Continuity
gems.insight: Fasting was prescribed to 'those before you' (alladhina min qablikum), indicating Jews, Christians, and other faith communities practiced forms of fasting for spiritual purification.
gems.line: Communities of faith before you fasted to be purified. You are inheriting, not inventing.

lines.text: I have submitted to the Lord of all the worlds.
The cow God asked for was free; the cow their questions built cost its weight in gold.
Obedience was always the shortest road; only our questions ever made it long.

2:183.morning: Ramadan begins. The fast written for those before you is now written for you - taqwa is its aim.
2:183.night: The first day of Ramadan closes. Fasting was written for you, and its purpose - taqwa - has begun.

21:73.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ أَئِمَّةًۭ يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِمْ فِعْلَ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَإِقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَإِيتَآءَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةِ ۖ وَكَانُوا۟ لَنَا عَٰبِدِينَ
21:73.translation: We made them imams, guiding by Our command, and We revealed to them [concerning] the performance of good deeds, the maintenance of prayers, and the giving of zakat, and they used to worship Us.

gems.title: Leaders Guiding
gems.insight: 'We made them leaders guiding by Our command' - Allah elevated them from being guided to being guides, from students to teachers of humanity.
gems.line: He raised them from guided to guides - the ones worth following were shaped by Him first.

gems.title: Inspired to Goodness
gems.insight: 'We inspired to them the doing of good deeds' - Allah directly inspires righteous actions in His chosen servants, making goodness natural to them.
gems.line: Goodness was made natural to them - He inspired the very doing of good in His chosen servants.

gems.title: Pillars Established
gems.insight: Allah lists specific acts: 'establishment of prayer and giving of zakah' - showing that true worship combines spiritual devotion (salah) with social responsibility (zakah).
gems.line: Prayer beside zakah in one breath - devotion to Him and duty to people are one worship.

21:73.morning: It is the birth of Imam Hasan - the verse gives the day its frame: leaders who guide by His command.
21:73.night: The birth of Imam Hasan closes the day on the verse's pattern: guides appointed by Him, worshippers of Him.

33:23.arabic: مِّنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ رِجَالٌۭ صَدَقُوا۟ مَا عَٰهَدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عَلَيْهِ ۖ فَمِنْهُم مَّن قَضَىٰ نَحْبَهُۥ وَمِنْهُم مَّن يَنتَظِرُ ۖ وَمَا بَدَّلُوا۟ تَبْدِيلًۭا
33:23.translation: Among the faithful are men who fulfill what they have pledged to Allah: there are some among them who have fulfilled their pledge, and some of them who still wait, and they have not changed in the least,

gems.title: Truthful Men
gems.insight: 'Rijal sadaqu' - men who were true to their covenant with Allah. They fulfilled their promises to defend Islam regardless of personal cost.
gems.line: Sidq at this level is a covenant kept with Allah - truthfulness proven by cost, not by claim.

gems.title: Fulfilled Vow
gems.insight: 'Man qada nahbahu' - those who fulfilled their vow (through martyrdom). Some believers gave their lives in devotion, completing their covenant with Allah.
gems.line: 'Some fulfilled their vow' - devotion carried to its completion, the covenant honored to the end.

gems.title: Those Awaiting
gems.insight: 'Man yantazir' - others await their turn to fulfill their covenant. They remain ready and committed, anticipating their opportunity to serve.
gems.line: 'Some await' - readiness is also faithfulness; the committed stay steady before their turn.

gems.title: No Alteration
gems.insight: 'Ma baddalu tabdilan' - they did not alter their commitment at all. Unlike hypocrites who change with circumstances, true believers remain steadfast.
gems.line: Circumstances shift and hypocrites shift with them - the truthful altered nothing at all.

33:23.morning: On the day of Imam Ali's martyrdom, the verse speaks its words: men true to what they promised Allah.
33:23.night: The night of Imam Ali's martyrdom closes on the verse he lived: true to the promise, altering nothing.

97:1.arabic: بِّسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ فِى لَيْلَةِ ٱلْقَدْرِ
97:1.translation: Indeed We sent it down on the Night of Ordainment.

gems.title: Divine Revelation
gems.insight: The Quran was 'sent down' (anzalna) - emphasizing its divine origin from Allah to humanity, not a human creation but a celestial gift.
gems.line: Anzalna settles the Qur'an's origin - sent down from Him, a gift given, not a book composed.

gems.title: Night of Decree
gems.insight: Laylat al-Qadr (Night of Decree/Power) is when the Quran was first revealed, marking the most blessed night when divine destiny is written and mercy overflows.
gems.line: Laylat al-Qadr is when destinies are set down and mercy pours - the night the Qur'an came down in.

gems.title: We Sent Down
gems.insight: The plural 'We' (inna) is the royal plural used by Allah, emphasizing His majesty and authority - the Sovereign King revealing His will to humanity.
gems.line: 'We sent it down' - the plural of majesty; the Sovereign Himself stands behind the sending.

97:1.morning: Laylat al-Qadr arrives with this day - the night of the Qur'an's descent, when mercy overflows.
97:1.night: This is the night itself - the Qur'an descended in hours like these, and destinies are being written.

gems.title: Has Succeeded
gems.insight: The emphatic 'qad aflaha' (has certainly succeeded) announces definitive victory for those who purify themselves - success guaranteed by Allah Himself.
gems.line: Qad aflaha is a verdict already given - the purified one's success is declared by Allah Himself.

gems.title: Who Purifies
gems.insight: The verb 'tazakkaa' (purifies himself) indicates active self-purification - cleansing the soul from sins, ego, and spiritual impurities.
gems.line: Tazakka is work done on yourself - purification is chosen and carried out, not merely received.

gems.title: Tazkiyah Path
gems.insight: Tazkiyah (purification) is comprehensive - purifying beliefs from shirk, hearts from diseases like envy, and actions from sins. It's holistic spiritual development.
gems.line: Tazkiyah runs the whole depth - creed cleared of shirk, the heart of envy, the day's acts of sin.

87:14.morning: Eid al-Fitr dawns on the verse's verdict: he has succeeded who purified himself - a month's work crowned.
87:14.night: Eid's night settles on the verse's verdict - the purified soul, and success declared by Him.

2:198.arabic: لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَبْتَغُوا۟ فَضْلًۭا مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ ۚ فَإِذَآ أَفَضْتُم مِّنْ عَرَفَٰتٍۢ فَٱذْكُرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عِندَ ٱلْمَشْعَرِ ٱلْحَرَامِ ۖ وَٱذْكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَىٰكُمْ وَإِن كُنتُم مِّن قَبْلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
2:198.translation: There is no sin upon you in seeking your Lord’s bounty [during the hajj season]. Then when you stream out of ‘Arafat remember Allah at the Holy Mash‘ar, and remember Him as He has guided you, and earlier you were indeed among the astray.

gems.title: Trade During Hajj
gems.insight: The verse clarifies that there is no sin in seeking Allah's bounty (trade and commerce) during the Hajj season. Early Muslims wondered if conducting business during pilgrimage was inappropriate. This verse establishes that earning a livelihood and fulfilling Hajj can coexist - Islam does not require abandoning worldly responsibilities for worship.
gems.line: Earning a living and seeking Him were never rivals - even at Hajj, bounty and worship coexist.

gems.title: Standing at Arafat
gems.insight: Arafat is the essential pillar of Hajj - the Prophet said 'Hajj is Arafat.' The verse instructs pilgrims that after departing from Arafat, they should remember Allah at Mash'ar al-Haram (Muzdalifah). This standing represents humanity's gathering on the Day of Judgment, where all stand equal before Allah regardless of status or wealth.
gems.line: At Arafat everyone stands the same - a rehearsal for the Day all wealth and rank fall away.

gems.title: Remembrance at Muzdalifah
gems.insight: Al-Mash'ar al-Haram (the Sacred Monument) at Muzdalifah is where pilgrims spend the night after Arafat, engaging in dhikr (remembrance of Allah). This overnight stay under the open sky, surrounded by fellow pilgrims, deepens the spiritual connection established at Arafat and prepares hearts for the rituals of Eid day.
gems.line: The night at Muzdalifah is dhikr under the open sky - stillness that seals what Arafat began.

gems.title: Divine Guidance
gems.insight: The verse reminds pilgrims to remember Allah 'as He guided you, for indeed you were before that among those astray.' This acknowledgment of previous misguidance cultivates humility and gratitude. The guidance to Hajj, to Islam, to the correct path - none of it was earned, but was Allah's mercy and gift to be appreciated.
gems.line: Guidance was never earned - it was given while you were astray. Humility is remembering that.

lines.text: I have submitted to the Lord of all the worlds.
The cow God asked for was free; the cow their questions built cost its weight in gold.
Obedience was always the shortest road; only our questions ever made it long.

2:198.morning: It is the Day of Arafah. Today's standing is remembrance: He guided you when you were astray.
2:198.night: Arafah closes with remembrance: you were once astray, and He guided you. That is tonight's thanks.

37:107.translation: Then We ransomed him with a great sacrifice,

gems.title: Divine Ransom
gems.insight: Allah Himself provided the ransom (fidya) - the sacrifice was not Ibrahim's provision but a divine gift. The test was about willingness, not actual bloodshed.
gems.line: The ransom was His provision, not Ibrahim's - the test measured willingness, never bloodshed.

gems.title: Great Sacrifice
gems.insight: The ram is called 'azim (great/magnificent) - its greatness comes not from its physical size but from its role in this pivotal moment of prophetic history.
gems.line: The ram is called azim for its role, not its size - greatness here is assigned by the moment.

gems.title: Symbolic Substitution
gems.insight: The ransom established the principle of animal sacrifice replacing human sacrifice - marking Islam's rejection of bloodshed for bloodshed and affirming the sanctity of human life.
gems.line: The ransom replaced human sacrifice for good - the sanctity of human life is written into this rite.

gems.title: Prophetic Legacy
gems.insight: This sacrifice became the foundation for Eid al-Adha, eternally commemorating submission and trust in Allah across all Muslim generations.
gems.line: Every Eid al-Adha flows from this verse - one act of submission, commemorated across generations.

37:107.morning: Eid al-Adha begins. Today remembers the ransom - Allah Himself provided what Ibrahim's test required.
37:107.night: Eid al-Adha closes. What He asked of Ibrahim was willingness, and what He gave back was the ransom.

5:67.arabic: ۞ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلرَّسُولُ بَلِّغْ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ ۖ وَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلْ فَمَا بَلَّغْتَ رِسَالَتَهُۥ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
5:67.translation: O Apostle! Communicate that which has been sent down to you from your Lord, and if you do not, you will not have communicated His message, and Allah shall protect you from the people. Indeed Allah does not guide the faithless lot.

gems.title: Complete Delivery
gems.insight: The Prophet is commanded to announce everything revealed without omission. If he doesn't convey it all, he hasn't truly delivered the message at all.
gems.line: The message had no optional parts - leaving one piece out would have left all of it undelivered.

gems.title: Allah's Protection
gems.insight: Allah promises to protect the Messenger from people. Despite opposition and threats, divine guardianship ensures the message reaches completion.
gems.line: 'Allah will protect you from the people' - the announcement went out under divine guard.

gems.title: Crucial Declaration
gems.insight: Scholars note this verse often refers to the declaration of Wilayah at Ghadir Khumm - a message so important that without it, the entire mission would be incomplete.
gems.line: At Ghadir Khumm the wilayah was declared - the one message the whole mission waited on.

lines.text: He whose mawla I am - whose guardian and master I am - this Ali is his mawla.
This day I have perfected for you your religion, and completed My favor upon you...
You renew the oldest pledge every time you stand to pray: we hear, and we obey.

5:67.morning: It is the day of Ghadeer - the Messenger was told: convey it, or the message is not conveyed.
5:67.night: Ghadeer closes: the message was delivered in full, under the protection He promised His Messenger.

3:61.arabic: فَمَنْ حَآجَّكَ فِيهِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ فَقُلْ تَعَالَوْا۟ نَدْعُ أَبْنَآءَنَا وَأَبْنَآءَكُمْ وَنِسَآءَنَا وَنِسَآءَكُمْ وَأَنفُسَنَا وَأَنفُسَكُمْ ثُمَّ نَبْتَهِلْ فَنَجْعَل لَّعْنَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَى ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
3:61.translation: Should anyone argue with you concerning him, after the knowledge that has come to you, say, ‘Come! Let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, our souls and your souls, then let us pray earnestly, and call down Allah’s curse upon the liars.’

gems.title: Mubahala
gems.insight: The event of Mubahala where the Prophet was commanded to gather his family and invoke Allah's curse upon liars. This establishes the spiritual authority of the Ahlul Bayt.
gems.line: When truth was challenged, the Prophet brought his family - the Ahlul Bayt stand where truth stands.

gems.title: Truth's Confidence
gems.insight: The willingness to invoke mutual cursing demonstrates absolute confidence in truth. The Prophet's certainty was so strong he was ready to stake everything on it.
gems.line: Certainty shows in what it will stake. The Prophet was ready to put everything behind the truth.

gems.title: After Knowledge
gems.insight: The verse addresses those who persist in argumentation after clear knowledge has been presented. Rejecting truth after evidence is a grave spiritual error.
gems.line: After clear knowledge arrives, endless argument stops being a search - the verse marks that line.

lines.text: When the truth was put on trial, God reached not for a sword but for a purified family.
One word - purified - travels from Maryam's prayer-niche to the five beneath the cloak.

3:61.morning: It is Mubahala. Challenged after clear knowledge, the Prophet answered by bringing his family forward.
3:61.night: Mubahala closes: the Prophet's proof was the people he brought - his nearest, standing beside the truth.

76:8.arabic: وَيُطْعِمُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ مِسْكِينًۭا وَيَتِيمًۭا وَأَسِيرًا
76:8.translation: For the love of Him, they feed the needy, the orphan and the prisoner,

gems.title: Love-Based Charity
gems.insight: The phrase 'in spite of love for it' reveals that true charity means giving what you cherish, not just excess wealth you don't need.
gems.line: 'In spite of love for it' - real giving parts with what you still want, not what you were done with.

gems.title: Three Recipients
gems.insight: The Quran specifies three groups worthy of charity: the needy (miskin), orphans (yatim), and captives (asir), representing different forms of vulnerability.
gems.line: The verse names three - the needy, the orphan, the captive - vulnerability in its different forms.

gems.title: Food as Love
gems.insight: Feeding others is emphasized as a primary act of righteousness, recognizing that physical hunger is the most immediate form of human suffering.
gems.line: Feeding someone meets the most immediate human need - righteousness that begins with hunger.

76:8.morning: It is the day of Surah al-Insan - food given out of love for Him to the needy, the orphan, the captive.
76:8.night: The day of al-Insan closes on its example - cherished food handed over, out of love for Him.

lines.text: This is between Me and My servant - and My servant shall have what he asked.
The prayer God taught you to pray, He answers: the asking and the giving are one motion.
Al-Fatiha ends with a plea, guide us - and the very next page of the Qur'an is the answer.
I have submitted to the Lord of all the worlds.
The cow God asked for was free; the cow their questions built cost its weight in gold.
Obedience was always the shortest road; only our questions ever made it long.
We feed you only for the Face of God - we desire from you no repayment, and no thanks.
The intention of the believer is better than his deed.
lines.source: The Messenger of God ﷺ - al-Kafi

lines.text: Some deeds stay pure the way secrets stay secrets: untold.
When the truth was put on trial, God reached not for a sword but for a purified family.
One word - purified - travels from Maryam's prayer-niche to the five beneath the cloak.
Taste this, Ali - taste the fire. This is for the one who fails the widow and the orphan.
A right on a page protects no one; every right is a trust placed in someone's hands.
Obedience closes the distance that love alone cannot close.
They are Fatima, her father, her husband, and her sons.
I did not create a built sky... except for the love of these Five beneath the cloak.
lines.source: His word to the angels - Hadith al-Kisa

lines.text: The sky you have lived your whole life under was raised for the five beneath that cloak.
He whose mawla I am - whose guardian and master I am - this Ali is his mawla.
This day I have perfected for you your religion, and completed My favor upon you...
You renew the oldest pledge every time you stand to pray: we hear, and we obey.
I love not those that set.
A heart made for God can chase the setting lights its whole life and never once feel held.
There was never a second pile: a whole life, prayer to final breath, turned one direction.
Patience upon Your decree, O my Lord. There is no god but You.
lines.source: Imam al-Husayn - Maqtal al-Husayn of al-Muqarram

lines.text: I complain of my anguish and my grief only to God.
Patience has three stations: to endure the decree, to accept it, to find peace within it.
You said yes once, before you can remember; your life is the second time you are asked.
They walked in as Pharaoh's hired magicians at sunrise; before sunset they were martyrs.
Pride, heedlessness, or a slow letting-go: every fall in al-A'raf is one promise slipping.
And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw.
Badr was won before the first arrow: the victory was God's to give.
When the outcome was never yours to carry, you are free to pour yourself out completely.
Our intercession will not reach one who takes the prayer lightly.
lines.source: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq - al-Amali of al-Saduq

lines.text: Prostrate - and draw near.
You have never once prayed unanswered - He answers the Fatiha line for line.
Before you ever turned toward God, He had already turned toward you.
The one who repents of a sin is as one with no sin at all.
Every road away from God turns, and leads back into His mercy.
My servant keeps drawing near to Me with voluntary acts until I love him...
Pharaoh did not run out of mercy; he ran out of moments when a yes could mean anything.
Only one city ever turned in time; this surah carries its prophet's name as the proof.
I praise God with the best of praise, and I thank Him in ease and in hardship.
Now you have thanked Me - now that you know that even the thanks is from Me.
Thanks is the one debt that grows by being paid.
Hud and its sisters have grayed me.
The same surah that grayed the Prophet was built, story by story, to steady his heart.
Fear needs a second power. Hud counted the powers in the world and came to one.
No blame upon you today. May God forgive you, and He is the most merciful of the merciful.
Beautiful patience is the certainty that God keeps an account no darkness can erase.
Every pit was a road; from the well to the throne, not one hour was wasted.
Whoever feared Me in the world, I make him secure on the Day of Resurrection.
A little deed with taqwa is worth more than a great deal without it.
Taqwa is not the size of what you do - it is what you refuse when no one would know.
Truly, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest.
I am the warner, and Ali is the guide after me.
The foam rides loud on the flood, and it goes; what benefits people remains in the earth.
A good word is like a good tree: its root is firm, and its branch reaches into the sky.
I am the prayer of my father Ibrahim.
What is planted with God in dead ground is never wasted; it grows while you are gone.
O God, You are my trust in every distress, and my hope in every hardship.
And when you have resolved, rely upon God. Indeed God loves those who rely.
Trust placed in Him, not in the outcome, cannot be broken by the outcome.
Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, it is We who will guard it.
Gracious forgiveness is pardon without reproach.
The surah says 'secure' twice: on walls carved into rock, and at a door He opens in peace.
They recognize the blessing of Allah - then they deny it.
Asked what a good life means in the Qur'an, he said: it is contentment.
The surah is named not for the pouring, but for the one who received it rightly.
I saw nothing but beauty.
lines.source: Sayyida Zaynab - al-Luhuf of Ibn Tawus

lines.text: And worship your Lord until certainty comes to you.
Certainty has three depths: to know the fire by its smoke, to see it, to stand within it.
People are asleep, and when they die they wake.
"Peace" - a word from a Merciful Lord.
An awake heart runs toward the truth; it never quite learned how to walk.
None of Your favors, my Lord, do I deny.
Guidance was prepared before you existed, the way a cradle is made ready before a birth.
Everything passes; what remains is not a cold survivor but generosity that stays.
From the furthest star to the water in your throat: one hand.
The One who will not let the bird drop for a single moment is the One holding you.
Al-Mulk at night sends ahead the one voice that will still speak when yours has stopped.
Truly, We have given you al-Kawthar.
God answered the cruelest taunt with a daughter, and through her line filled the earth.
The abundance may already be in your house, in a form the world has not learned to count.
